subject: Math
title: Condition for Tangency (Line)
description: Line $y=mx+c$ touches circle $x^2+y^2=a^2$.
derivation:
Distance from center $(0,0)$ to line $mx - y + c = 0$ must equal radius $a$.
$p = \frac{|m(0) - 0 + c|}{\sqrt{m^2 + 1}} = a$.
$\frac{|c|}{\sqrt{1+m^2}} = a$.
Square both sides: $c^2 = a^2(1+m^2)$.

related_concepts.name: Tangent Equation
related_concepts.definition: $y = mx \pm a\sqrt{1+m^2}$.

subject: Math
title: Length of Common Chord
description: Length of chord shared by intersecting circles.
derivation:
1. Find Equation of Common Chord (Radical Axis): $S_1 - S_2 = 0$ (Line $L$).
2. Find perpendicular distance ($p$) from center $C_1$ to this line $L$.
3. Use Pythagoras in $\Delta C_1 M A$ (where M is midpoint of chord, A is intersection).
   $AM^2 + p^2 = r_1^2 \implies AM = \sqrt{r_1^2 - p^2}$.
4. Total Length = $2 \times AM$.

related_concepts.name: Intersection Condition
related_concepts.definition: $|r_1 - r_2| < d < r_1 + r_2$ (d is dist between centers).

subject: Math
title: Center & Radius (General Form)
description: Extract center and radius from the general equation. \(g, f, c\) = coefficients in \(x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0\); \(C\) = center, \(r\) = radius. Real circle needs \(g^2+f^2-c>0\).

subject: Math
title: Circle on Diameter Endpoints
description: Equation of circle with the segment joining two points as diameter. \((x_1,y_1)\) and \((x_2,y_2)\) = endpoints of the diameter.
derivation:
Any point \(P(x,y)\) on the circle subtends \(90^\circ\) at the diameter ends.
So slopes satisfy \(\frac{y-y_1}{x-x_1}\cdot\frac{y-y_2}{x-x_2} = -1\).
Cross-multiplying gives \((x-x_1)(x-x_2)+(y-y_1)(y-y_2)=0\).

subject: Math
title: Position of a Point
description: Locate a point relative to the circle. \(S_1 = x_1^2+y_1^2+2gx_1+2fy_1+c\) is the circle expression evaluated at \(P(x_1,y_1)\).

subject: Math
title: Line-Circle Intersection
visual_data: p < r \ (\text{secant}), \quad p = r \ (\text{tangent}), \quad p > r \ (\text{no cut})
description: Number of intersection points of a line with a circle via distance. \(p\) = perpendicular distance of center from the line, \(r\) = radius.

subject: Math
title: Tangent in Slope Form
description: Tangents of slope \(m\) to circle \(x^2+y^2=r^2\). \(m\) = slope, \(r\) = radius; point of contact \(\left(\mp\frac{rm}{\sqrt{1+m^2}}, \pm\frac{r}{\sqrt{1+m^2}}\right)\).
derivation:
Line \(y=mx+c\) is tangent if distance from origin \(=r\).
\(\frac{|c|}{\sqrt{1+m^2}} = r \implies c = \pm r\sqrt{1+m^2}\).

subject: Math
title: Normal to a Circle
description: Normal at point \((x_1,y_1)\) on \(x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0\); it always passes through the center. \(g,f\) = coefficients of the circle.

subject: Math
title: Pair of Tangents (SS1 = T^2)
description: Combined equation of the two tangents from external point \((x_1,y_1)\). \(S\)=circle expression, \(S_1\)=\(S\) at the point, \(T\)=tangent/chord-of-contact expression.

subject: Math
title: Angle Between Tangents from a Point
description: Angle \(\theta\) between the two tangents drawn from an external point. \(r\)=radius, \(\sqrt{S_1}\)=length of tangent from the point.
derivation:
Center \(C\), external point \(P\), point of contact \(A\), with \(\angle CAP = 90^\circ\).
Half-angle \(\frac{\theta}{2}=\angle APC\), so \(\tan\frac{\theta}{2}=\frac{CA}{PA}=\frac{r}{\sqrt{S_1}}\).

subject: Math
title: Family of Circles (Line)
description: Circles through intersection of circle \(S=0\) and line \(L=0\). \(\lambda\) = real parameter chosen by an extra condition.

subject: Math
title: Family of Circles (Two Circles)
description: Circles through the intersection of two circles \(S_1=0\), \(S_2=0\). \(\lambda\)=parameter; \(\lambda=-1\) gives the radical axis (a line).

subject: Math
title: Circle Through Two Points
visual_data: (x - x_1)(x - x_2) + (y - y_1)(y - y_2) + \lambda \begin{vmatrix} x & y & 1 \\ x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0
description: Family of circles through points \(A(x_1,y_1)\), \(B(x_2,y_2)\). The determinant is the line \(AB\); \(\lambda\)=parameter.

subject: Math
title: Distance Between Centers (Positions)
visual_data: \begin{aligned} d > r_1 + r_2 &: \text{separate (4 tangents)} \\ d = r_1 + r_2 &: \text{external touch (3)} \\ |r_1 - r_2| < d < r_1 + r_2 &: \text{intersect (2)} \\ d = |r_1 - r_2| &: \text{internal touch (1)} \\ d < |r_1 - r_2| &: \text{one inside (0)} \end{aligned}
description: Relative position and number of common tangents of two circles. \(d\)=distance between centers, \(r_1,r_2\)=radii.

subject: Math
title: Point of Contact (Touching Circles)
visual_data: P = \frac{r_1 C_2 + r_2 C_1}{r_1 + r_2} \ (\text{ext}), \quad \frac{r_1 C_2 - r_2 C_1}{r_1 - r_2} \ (\text{int})
description: Point where two touching circles meet, by section formula on the line of centers. \(C_1,C_2\)=centers, \(r_1,r_2\)=radii.

subject: Math
title: Length of Direct Common Tangent
description: Length of a direct (external) common tangent between two circles. \(d\)=distance between centers, \(r_1,r_2\)=radii.

subject: Math
title: Radical Center
description: Common point of the three radical axes of three circles; equal tangent lengths to all three. \(S_1,S_2,S_3\)=the three circle expressions.

subject: Math
title: Tangent at Origin
description: Tangent to \(x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy=0\) (passing through origin, \(c=0\)) at the origin. \(g,f\)=coefficients.

subject: Math
title: Intercepts on Axes
description: Lengths the circle cuts on the x-axis and y-axis. \(g,f,c\)=coefficients; x-intercept needs \(g^2>c\), y-intercept needs \(f^2>c\).
derivation:
Put \(y=0\): \(x^2+2gx+c=0\); difference of roots \(=\sqrt{(2g)^2-4c}=2\sqrt{g^2-c}\).
Similarly put \(x=0\) for the y-axis.

subject: Math
title: Equation of Chord Joining Two Parametric Points
description: Chord joining points at angles \(\alpha,\beta\) on \(x^2+y^2=r^2\). \(\alpha,\beta\)=parameters, \(r\)=radius.

subject: Math
title: Locus of Midpoints / Diameter of a Chord System
description: Diameter bisecting all chords of slope \(m\): passes through center \((h,k)\) perpendicular to the chords. \(m\)=common chord slope; locus of midpoints is this line.

subject: Math
title: Linear Differential Equation
description: First order linear ODE where $P$ and $Q$ are functions of $x$ (or constants).
derivation:
To solve, multiply by Integrating Factor (IF) $e^{\int P dx}$.
$e^{\int P dx} \frac{dy}{dx} + P e^{\int P dx} y = Q e^{\int P dx}$
The LHS becomes the derivative of product: $\frac{d}{dx} (y \cdot e^{\int P dx})$.
Integrate both sides:
$y \cdot (IF) = \int (Q \cdot IF) dx + C$.

related_concepts.name: Bernoulli's Equation
related_concepts.definition: Reducible to linear form: $\frac{dy}{dx} + Py = Qy^n$.

subject: Math
title: Homogeneous Equation
description: ODE where the RHS is a homogeneous function of degree 0.
derivation:
Let $y = vx$. Then $\frac{dy}{dx} = v + x \frac{dv}{dx}$.
Substitute into ODE: $v + x \frac{dv}{dx} = F(v)$.
Separate variables: $x \frac{dv}{dx} = F(v) - v$.
$\frac{dv}{F(v) - v} = \frac{dx}{x}$.
Integrate both sides.

related_concepts.name: Homogeneous Function
related_concepts.definition: $f(\lambda x, \lambda y) = \lambda^n f(x, y)$.

subject: Math
title: Bernoulli's Equation
description: Non-linear ODE reducible to linear form.
derivation:
1. Divide by $y^n$: $y^{-n} y' + P y^{1-n} = Q$.
2. Substitution: Let $z = y^{1-n}$.
   Differentiation: $z' = (1-n) y^{-n} y'$.
3. Replace terms: $\frac{z'}{1-n} + Pz = Q$.
4. Standard Linear Form: $z' + (1-n)P z = (1-n)Q$. Solve using IF.

related_concepts.name: Reduction to Linear
related_concepts.definition: Method of transforming non-linear equations using substitution.

subject: Math
title: Newton's Law of Cooling
description: Rate of cooling is proportional to temperature difference with surroundings.
derivation:
Physical Law: Rate of heat loss $\propto \Delta T$.
$-\frac{dT}{dt} \propto (T - T_s)$.
$\frac{dT}{dt} = -k(T - T_s)$.
Separable form: $\frac{dT}{T-T_s} = -k dt$.
Solution: $\ln(T-T_s) = -kt + C \implies T(t) = T_s + C e^{-kt}$.

related_concepts.name: Exponential Decay
related_concepts.definition: Process where quantity decreases at a rate proportional to its current value.

subject: Math
title: Orthogonal Trajectory
description: Family of curves intersecting given family at right angles.
derivation:
1. Form differential equation of given family: $f(x, y, y') = 0$.
2. Condition for orthogonality: Product of slopes $m_1 m_2 = -1$.
   So, replace $y'$ with $-1/y'$.
3. Solve the new Differential Equation to get the orthogonal family.

related_concepts.name: Equipotential Lines
related_concepts.definition: Orthogonal trajectories to electric field lines.

subject: Math
title: Order & Degree
description: Defines order and degree of a differential equation. Order \(=\) order of highest-order derivative present; degree \(=\) power of the highest-order derivative after the equation is made a polynomial in derivatives (free of radicals/fractions in derivatives). Degree is defined only when so expressible.

subject: Math
title: Variable Separable
description: Solves equations where variables can be separated. \(f(x)\)=function of \(x\) only, \(g(y)\)=function of \(y\) only, \(C\)=arbitrary constant.

subject: Math
title: Reducible to Separable
visual_data: \frac{dy}{dx} = f(ax + by + c) \implies \text{put } t = ax + by + c
description: Substitution for equations whose RHS depends only on the linear combination \(ax+by+c\). Then \(\frac{dt}{dx}=a+b\frac{dy}{dx}\), giving a separable equation in \(t,x\). \(a,b,c\)=constants.

subject: Math
title: Integrating Factor (Linear)
visual_data: \text{I.F.} = e^{\int P\, dx}, \quad y \cdot (\text{I.F.}) = \int Q\,(\text{I.F.})\, dx + C
description: Solution of linear DE \(\frac{dy}{dx}+Py=Q\). \(P,Q\)=functions of \(x\); I.F.=integrating factor; \(C\)=arbitrary constant.
derivation:
\(\frac{dy}{dx}+Py=Q\)
Multiply by \(\mu=e^{\int P dx}\): \(\mu y' + \mu P y = \mu Q\)
LHS \(=\frac{d}{dx}(\mu y)\) since \(\mu'=\mu P\)
Integrate: \(\mu y = \int \mu Q\, dx + C\)

subject: Math
title: Linear in x
description: Linear DE with \(x\) as dependent variable; use when \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) form is non-linear but \(\frac{dx}{dy}\) is linear. \(P,Q\)=functions of \(y\); solution \(x\cdot\text{I.F.}=\int Q\,\text{I.F.}\,dy + C\).

subject: Math
title: Exact Differential Equation
visual_data: M\,dx + N\,dy = 0 \text{ is exact} \iff \frac{\partial M}{\partial y} = \frac{\partial N}{\partial x}
description: Exactness condition; solution found by \(\int M\,dx + \int(\text{terms of } N \text{ free of } x)\,dy = C\). \(M,N\)=functions of \(x,y\).

subject: Math
title: Useful Exact Differentials
description: Standard differentials for grouping terms in exact-type DEs. Also \(d(xy)=x\,dy+y\,dx\); \(d\left(\tan^{-1}\tfrac{y}{x}\right)=\frac{x\,dy-y\,dx}{x^2+y^2}\); \(d\left(\ln\tfrac{y}{x}\right)=\frac{x\,dy-y\,dx}{xy}\).

subject: Math
title: Non-Homogeneous Linear Lines
visual_data: \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{a_1 x + b_1 y + c_1}{a_2 x + b_2 y + c_2}
description: Reducible to homogeneous. If \(\frac{a_1}{a_2}\ne\frac{b_1}{b_2}\): shift origin to intersection \((h,k)\) via \(x=X+h,\ y=Y+k\). If \(\frac{a_1}{a_2}=\frac{b_1}{b_2}\): put \(t=a_2 x+b_2 y\) (separable). \(a_i,b_i,c_i\)=constants.

subject: Math
title: Clairaut's Equation
description: General solution obtained by replacing \(p\) with constant \(c\): \(y=cx+f(c)\). Singular solution from eliminating \(p\) between \(y=px+f(p)\) and \(x+f'(p)=0\). \(p\)=slope \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).

subject: Math
title: Number of Arbitrary Constants
visual_data: \text{No. of arbitrary constants} = \text{order of the differential equation}
description: The general solution of an \(n\)th-order DE contains exactly \(n\) independent arbitrary constants; eliminating \(n\) constants from a family of curves gives a DE of order \(n\).

subject: Math
title: Formation of Differential Equation
visual_data: \text{Differentiate } y = f(x, c_1, \dots, c_n) \ n \text{ times, then eliminate } c_1,\dots,c_n
description: To form the DE of a family of curves with \(n\) arbitrary constants, differentiate \(n\) times and eliminate the constants to get an \(n\)th-order DE. \(c_1,\dots,c_n\)=parameters of the family.

subject: Math
title: Homogeneous Substitution
description: Standard substitution that converts a homogeneous DE into variable-separable form. \(v=\frac{y}{x}\); after substitution \(\int\frac{dv}{F(v)-v}=\int\frac{dx}{x}+C\).

subject: Math
title: Bernoulli Substitution
description: Reduces Bernoulli's equation to linear form by dividing by \(y^n\) and substituting \(t=y^{1-n}\), giving \(\frac{dt}{dx}+(1-n)Pt=(1-n)Q\). \(P,Q\)=functions of \(x\), \(n\ne0,1\).

subject: Math
title: Growth & Decay Law
description: Exponential growth/decay (population, radioactive decay, etc.). \(y_0\)=initial amount, \(k>0\) growth and \(k<0\) decay, \(t\)=time.

subject: Math
title: Slope / Tangent-Normal DE
description: Sets up geometric DEs from tangent/normal conditions. Subtangent \(=\frac{y}{dy/dx}\), subnormal \(=y\frac{dy}{dx}\); used when a curve's geometric property gives a DE.

subject: Math
title: Periodicity of f(ax+b)
description: If $f(x)$ has period $T$, then $f(ax+b)$ has a modified period.
derivation:
Definition of period $T'$: $f(a(x+T') + b) = f(ax+b)$.
Since $f(X)$ repeats every $T$, we need the argument to increase by $T$.
$a(x+T') + b - (ax+b) = T$.
$ax + aT' + b - ax - b = T$.
$aT' = T \implies T' = T/|a|$.

related_concepts.name: Fundamental Period
related_concepts.definition: The smallest positive value of $T$ for which $f(x+T)=f(x)$.

subject: Math
title: Power Set Cardinality
description: Total number of subsets of a set A with n elements.
derivation:
Let set A have $n$ elements.
To form a subset, for each element $x \in A$, there are exactly 2 choices:
1. Include $x$ in the subset.
2. Exclude $x$ from the subset.
Total combinations = $2 \times 2 \times \dots \times 2$ ($n$ times) = $2^n$.

related_concepts.name: Binomial Theorem
related_concepts.definition: $\sum_{r=0}^n \binom{n}{r} = 2^n$ (Sum of all possible selections).

subject: Math
title: Cartesian Product Cardinality
description: Total number of ordered pairs $(a, b)$ where $a \in A, b \in B$.
derivation:
Let $n(A) = p$ and $n(B) = q$.
For each of the $p$ elements in A, we can pair it with any of the $q$ elements in B.
This forms $p$ groups of $q$ pairs.
Total pairs = $p + p + \dots$ ($q$ times? No, $p$ times $q$) = $p \times q$.

related_concepts.name: Ordered Pair
related_concepts.definition: A pair $(a, b)$ where order matters; $(a, b) \neq (b, a)$ unless $a=b$.

subject: Math
title: Total Number of Relations
description: Number of possible relations from set A ($m$ elements) to set B ($n$ elements).
derivation:
A relation is defined as a subset of the Cartesian product $A \times B$.
Number of elements in $A \times B$ is $mn$.
The number of subsets of a set with $k$ elements is $2^k$.
Substituting $k = mn$, Total Relations = $2^{mn}$.

related_concepts.name: Empty Relation
related_concepts.definition: The relation containing no ordered pairs (subset $\phi$).

subject: Math
title: Number of Reflexive Relations
description: Relations on set A where every element is related to itself.
derivation:
Total pairs in $A \times A$ is $n^2$.
Diagonal pairs $(a,a)$ are $n$. Non-diagonal pairs are $n^2 - n$.
For reflexivity, all $n$ diagonal pairs MUST be included (1 choice each).
The remaining $n^2 - n$ pairs can be either included or excluded (2 choices each).
Total = $1^n \times 2^{n^2-n} = 2^{n(n-1)}$.

related_concepts.name: Identity Relation
related_concepts.definition: Relation containing ONLY the diagonal pairs $\{(a,a) \forall a \in A\}$.

subject: Math
title: Number of Symmetric Relations
description: Relations where $(a,b) \in R \implies (b,a) \in R$.
derivation:
Pairs in $A \times A$ can be grouped:
1. Diagonal elements $(a,a)$: $n$ pairs. Each has 2 choices (in/out).
2. Off-diagonal pairs $\{(a,b), (b,a)\}$: $(n^2-n)/2$ sets. For symmetry, they must be selected together (either both in or both out).
Total choices = $2^n \times 2^{(n^2-n)/2} = 2^{(2n + n^2 - n)/2} = 2^{n(n+1)/2}$.

related_concepts.name: Upper Triangular Matrix
related_concepts.definition: Analogy to determining independent entries in a symmetric matrix.

subject: Math
title: Number of One-One Functions
description: Injective maps from set A ($m$ elements) to set B ($n$ elements). Valid if $n \ge m$.
derivation:
Let elements of A be $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_m$.
$a_1$ has $n$ choices in B.
$a_2$ has $n-1$ choices (cannot match $a_1$'s image).
$a_3$ has $n-2$ choices.
...
$a_m$ has $n-(m-1)$ choices.
Total = $n(n-1)\dots(n-m+1) = ^nP_m$.

related_concepts.name: Pigeonhole Principle
related_concepts.definition: If $m > n$, at least one element in B must be mapped to twice, so 0 one-one functions.

subject: Math
title: Number of Onto Functions
description: Surjective maps from A ($m$) to B ($n$). Requires $m \ge n$.
derivation:
Total functions = $n^m$.
Subtract functions that miss at least 1 element of B: $\binom{n}{1}(n-1)^m$.
Add back functions missing at least 2 (double counted): $\binom{n}{2}(n-2)^m$.
Using Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion:
$N = n^m - \binom{n}{1}(n-1)^m + \binom{n}{2}(n-2)^m - \dots$

related_concepts.name: Stirling Numbers
related_concepts.definition: Related to partitioning set A into n non-empty subsets ($S(m,n) \times n!$).

subject: Math
title: Number of Bijections
description: One-one and Onto functions. Possible only if $n(A) = n(B) = n$.
derivation:
From A ($n$) to B ($n$).
For One-One: $^nP_n = n!$.
For Onto: Using formula with $m=n$: $n^n - \binom{n}{1}(n-1)^n \dots = n!$.
Simplest logic: First element has $n$ choices, second $n-1$, ..., last 1.
$n \times (n-1) \times \dots \times 1 = n!$.

related_concepts.name: Permutation
related_concepts.definition: A bijection from a set to itself is a permutation.

subject: Math
title: Inverse Function Existence
description: A function has an inverse iff it is One-One and Onto.
derivation:
1. One-One (Injection): Ensures $f^{-1}$ maps an output back to a *unique* input.
2. Onto (Surjection): Ensures $f^{-1}$ is defined for *all* elements in the codomain.
Graphically: Passes Horizontal Line Test.

related_concepts.name: Horizontal Line Test
related_concepts.definition: A geometric test to determine if a function is one-to-one.

subject: Math
title: Inclusion-Exclusion (2 sets)
visual_data: n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B)
description: Cardinality of the union of two finite sets. \(n(A)\)=elements in \(A\), \(n(A\cap B)\)=elements common to both.

subject: Math
title: De Morgan's Laws
visual_data: (A \cup B)' = A' \cap B' \quad (A \cap B)' = A' \cup B'
description: Complement of a union/intersection. \(A'\)=complement of \(A\) w.r.t. universal set \(U\).

subject: Math
title: Set Difference Identity
visual_data: A - B = A \cap B' = A - (A \cap B)
description: Elements in \(A\) but not in \(B\). \(B'\)=complement of \(B\); useful for converting differences to intersections.

subject: Math
title: Symmetric Difference
visual_data: A \Delta B = (A - B) \cup (B - A) = (A \cup B) - (A \cap B)
description: Elements in exactly one of \(A\) or \(B\). Commutative and associative; \(n(A\Delta B)=n(A)+n(B)-2n(A\cap B)\).

subject: Math
title: Distributive Laws of Sets
visual_data: \begin{aligned} A \cap (B \cup C) &= (A\cap B) \cup (A\cap C) \\ A \cup (B \cap C) &= (A\cup B) \cap (A\cup C) \end{aligned}
description: Intersection distributes over union and vice-versa. Core identities for simplifying set expressions.

subject: Math
title: Exactly / At-least Counts
visual_data: \begin{aligned} n(\text{exactly one}) &= n(A)+n(B)+n(C) -2\sum n(A\cap B) +3n(A\cap B\cap C) \\ n(\text{exactly two}) &= \sum n(A\cap B) - 3n(A\cap B\cap C) \end{aligned}
description: Counts of elements in exactly one / exactly two of three sets. \(\sum n(A\cap B)\)=sum of three pairwise intersections.

subject: Math
title: Number of Subsets & Proper Subsets
description: Total subsets and proper subsets of a set with \(n\) elements. Proper subset excludes the set itself.

subject: Math
title: Number of Equivalence Relations / Onto Maps
description: Equivalence relations on an \(n\)-set equal the Bell number \(B(n)\)=sum of Stirling numbers \(S(n,k)\) (partitions into \(k\) blocks).

subject: Math
title: Number of Anti-symmetric Relations
description: Anti-symmetric relations on a set with \(n\) elements. \(2^n\) from diagonal pairs, \(3\) choices per off-diagonal unordered pair.

subject: Math
title: Number of Functions (total)
description: Total functions from \(A\) (size \(m\)) to \(B\) (size \(n\)). Each of \(m\) domain elements has \(n\) image choices.

subject: Math
title: Domain Rules: Root, Log, Reciprocal
visual_data: \begin{aligned} \sqrt{g(x)} &: g(x) \ge 0 \\ \log_a g(x) &: g(x) > 0,\ a>0, a\ne 1 \\ \frac{1}{g(x)} &: g(x) \ne 0 \end{aligned}
description: Domain conditions for the three commonest function blocks. \(g(x)\)=inner expression; combine via intersection.

subject: Math
title: Composite Function
description: Function composition and inverse of a composite. Range of \(g\) must lie in domain of \(f\); composition is associative, not commutative.

subject: Math
title: Inverse Function Property
description: Defining identities of an inverse function. Graph of \(f^{-1}\) is reflection of \(f\) about \(y=x\); requires \(f\) bijective.

subject: Math
title: Even & Odd Function Decomposition
description: Any function on a symmetric domain splits into even + odd parts. Even: \(f(-x)=f(x)\); Odd: \(f(-x)=-f(x)\).

subject: Math
title: Periods of Trig Functions
visual_data: \sin x, \cos x, \sec x, \csc x : 2\pi \quad \tan x, \cot x : \pi
description: Fundamental periods of trig functions; \(|\sin x|, |\cos x|\) have period \(\pi\). Basis for the LCM rule on composites.

subject: Math
title: Functional Equation: f(x)f(1/x)
visual_data: f(x) f(1/x) = f(x) + f(1/x) \implies f(x) = 1 \pm x^{n}
description: Standard functional equation; the general solution is \(f(x)=1\pm x^{n}\). \(n\)=real constant fixed by extra data.

subject: Math
title: Functional Equation: f(x+y)
description: Cauchy's additive equation (continuous solution). \(k\)=slope \(=f(1)\); linear through origin.

subject: Math
title: Number of Many-One Functions
description: Many-one functions \(=\) total \(-\) one-one. \(m=|A|, n=|B|\); valid count needs \(m\le n\) for one-one to exist.

subject: Math
title: Number of Into Functions
description: Into functions \(=\) total \(-\) onto. \(N_{\text{onto}}=\sum_{k=0}^{n}(-1)^k\binom{n}{k}(n-k)^m\); \(m=|A|,n=|B|\).

subject: Math
title: Number of Constant Functions
description: Constant functions from \(A\) to \(B\): one per element of codomain. Each maps all of \(A\) to a single \(b\in B\).

subject: Math
title: Self-Inverse Linear Function
description: Condition for an involution among Mobius maps; such \(f\) is its own inverse. \(a,b,c\)=constants with \(a^2+bc\ne 0\).

subject: Math
title: Sum Formula (tan inverse)
description: Standard addition formula. Note condition: $xy < 1$.
derivation:
Let $A = \tan^{-1} x$ and $B = \tan^{-1} y$. So $x = \tan A, y = \tan B$.
$\tan(A+B) = \frac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A \tan B} = \frac{x+y}{1-xy}$.
Taking inverse: $A+B = \tan^{-1} \frac{x+y}{1-xy}$.
If $xy > 1$, the denominator becomes negative, shifting the angle quadrant, requiring adjustment ($\pi$).

related_concepts.name: Principal Branch
related_concepts.definition: Range of $\tan^{-1} x$ is $(-\pi/2, \pi/2)$.

subject: Math
title: 2 tan inverse x Formula
description: Fundamental conversion formulas.
derivation:
Put $x = \tan \theta$. Then $\theta = \tan^{-1} x$.
1. $\sin 2\theta = \frac{2\tan \theta}{1+\tan^2 \theta} = \frac{2x}{1+x^2}$.
   So $2\theta = \sin^{-1} \dots$
2. $\cos 2\theta = \frac{1-\tan^2 \theta}{1+\tan^2 \theta} = \frac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}$.
   So $2\theta = \cos^{-1} \dots$

related_concepts.name: Half Angle Formulas
related_concepts.definition: Trigonometric identities relating angle $2\theta$ to $\tan \theta$.

subject: Math
title: Negative Argument Identities
description: Behaviour of inverse trig functions for negative arguments (odd vs supplementary). \(x\)=argument. \(\sin^{-1},\tan^{-1},\text{cosec}^{-1}\) are odd; \(\cos^{-1},\cot^{-1},\sec^{-1}\) give the supplement.

subject: Math
title: Complementary Pairs
description: The three complementary-angle identities for inverse trig functions. \(x\)=argument; each pair sums to \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) over the stated domain.

subject: Math
title: tan inverse Sum with Sign Cases
description: Full case-split of the \(\tan^{-1}\) sum formula (corrects the principal-value branch). \(x,y\)=arguments. The \(\pm\pi\) correction is needed when \(xy>1\) since the result leaves the principal range.

subject: Math
title: tan inverse Difference Formula
description: Difference of two \(\tan^{-1}\) terms; add \(\pi\) (if \(x>0,y<0,xy<-1\)) or subtract \(\pi\) (if \(x<0,y>0,xy<-1\)) otherwise. \(x,y\)=arguments.

subject: Math
title: sin inverse Sum Formula
description: Sum of two \(\sin^{-1}\) terms, valid when \(x^2+y^2\le 1\) or (\(xy<0\) and \(x^2+y^2>1\)). \(x,y\in[-1,1]\). Outside this, add/subtract \(\pi\) and negate the bracket as needed.

subject: Math
title: 2 sin inverse x Formula
description: Double-angle form for \(\sin^{-1}\). \(x\)=argument. Outside the range use \(\pi-\sin^{-1}(\cdot)\) for \(x>\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\) and \(-\pi-\sin^{-1}(\cdot)\) for \(x<-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\).

subject: Math
title: 3 tan inverse x Formula
description: Triple-angle form for \(\tan^{-1}\). \(x\)=argument. Add \(\pi\) for \(x>\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\), subtract \(\pi\) for \(x<-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\).

subject: Math
title: 3 cos inverse x Formula
description: Triple-angle form for \(\cos^{-1}\). \(x\)=argument. For other sub-intervals of \([-1,1]\) adjust by \(2\pi\) so the result lands in \([0,\pi]\).

subject: Math
title: tan inverse to sin/cos Conversions
description: Rewriting \(\tan^{-1}x\) as \(\sin^{-1}\) or \(\cos^{-1}\) (for \(x\ge0\)). \(x\)=argument. Useful for combining ITF terms.

subject: Math
title: sin inverse to tan/cos Conversion
description: Rewriting \(\sin^{-1}x\) in terms of \(\cos^{-1}\) or \(\tan^{-1}\) for \(x\in[0,1)\). \(x\)=argument.

subject: Math
title: Half-Angle (Algebraic) Substitutions
description: The three standard \(2\tan^{-1}x\) reductions used to simplify radical/rational ITF expressions. \(x\)=argument. Note each has its own validity range.

subject: Math
title: Trig of Inverse Trig (Composite Values)
description: Evaluating a trig function of an inverse-trig argument via a right triangle. \(x\)=argument; results assume principal values (non-negative roots).

subject: Math
title: sin(sin inverse) vs sin inverse(sin) Identities
description: The cancellation identities hold ONLY when the angle lies in the principal range; otherwise reduce \(\theta\) first. \(x\)=value, \(\theta\)=angle.

subject: Math
title: sin inverse(sin x) Outside Principal Range
description: Reducing \(\sin^{-1}(\sin\theta)\) when \(\theta\) is outside \([-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}]\); the graph is a triangular wave. \(\theta\)=angle in radians.

subject: Math
title: Derivatives of Inverse Trig Functions
description: Standard derivatives of all six inverse trig functions (frequently tested with substitutions). \(x\)=variable; note co-functions carry a negative sign.

subject: Math
title: sin/cos inverse Sum to Pi/2 Special Result
description: A high-frequency special identity (and its \(\cos^{-1}\) analogue). \(x\)=argument; follows from \(\sqrt{1-x^2}=\cos(\sin^{-1}x)\).

subject: Math
title: Variance Formula
description: Mean of squares minus square of mean.
derivation:
Start with definition: $\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{n} \sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2$.
Expand square: $(x_i^2 - 2x_i\bar{x} + \bar{x}^2)$.
Sum each term:
$\frac{1}{n} [\sum x_i^2 - 2\bar{x}\sum x_i + \sum \bar{x}^2]$.
Substitute $\sum x_i = n\bar{x}$ and $\sum \bar{x}^2 = n\bar{x}^2$:
$\frac{1}{n} [\sum x_i^2 - 2n\bar{x}^2 + n\bar{x}^2] = \frac{\sum x_i^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2$.

related_concepts.name: Standard Deviation
related_concepts.definition: $\sigma = \sqrt{\text{Variance}}$.

subject: Math
title: Coefficient of Variation (CV)
description: Dimensionless measure of relative variability/dispersion.
derivation:
Standard Deviation ($\sigma$) has units of the data.
Mean ($\bar{x}$) has units of the data.
Ratio $\sigma/\bar{x}$ cancels units.
Multiply by 100 to express as percentage.
Used to compare consistency of two datasets with different units/means.

related_concepts.name: Consistency
related_concepts.definition: Lower CV implies higher consistency (less fluctuation relative to mean).

subject: Math
title: Combined Mean
description: Weighted average of two distinct groups of data.
derivation:
Definition of Mean: $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x}{n} \implies \sum x = n \bar{x}$.
Sum of Group 1: $S_1 = n_1 \bar{x}_1$.
Sum of Group 2: $S_2 = n_2 \bar{x}_2$.
Total Sum: $S_{total} = n_1 \bar{x}_1 + n_2 \bar{x}_2$.
Total Count: $N = n_1 + n_2$.
Combined Mean = $S_{total} / N$.

related_concepts.name: Weighted Mean
related_concepts.definition: General form where weights $w_i$ are assigned to values $x_i$.

subject: Math
title: Combined Variance
description: Variance of merged dataset. $d_1 = \bar{x}_1 - \bar{x}_{comb}$, $d_2 = \bar{x}_2 - \bar{x}_{comb}$.
derivation:
Variance definition: $\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum x^2}{n} - (\bar{x})^2 \implies \sum x^2 = n(\sigma^2 + \bar{x}^2)$.
Calculate $\sum x^2$ for both groups and add them to get Total Sum Squares.
$\sum x_{comb}^2 = n_1(\sigma_1^2 + \bar{x}_1^2) + n_2(\sigma_2^2 + \bar{x}_2^2)$.
New Variance = $\frac{\sum x_{comb}^2}{N} - (\bar{x}_{comb})^2$.
Simplifying this expression yields the formula involving deviation $d$.

related_concepts.name: Analysis of Variance
related_concepts.definition: Statistical method to analyze differences among group means.

subject: Math
title: Arithmetic Mean (Ungrouped)
description: Mean of raw (ungrouped) data. \(\bar{x}\)=arithmetic mean, \(x_i\)=observations, \(n\)=number of observations.

subject: Math
title: Mean (Frequency / Discrete)
description: Mean of a discrete frequency distribution. \(x_i\)=values, \(f_i\)=frequencies, \(N=\sum f_i\)=total frequency.

subject: Math
title: Mean — Assumed Mean Method
visual_data: \bar{x} = a + \frac{\sum f_i d_i}{\sum f_i}, \quad d_i = x_i - a
description: Shortcut mean using an assumed mean to ease arithmetic. \(a\)=assumed mean, \(d_i\)=deviation \(x_i-a\), \(f_i\)=frequency.

subject: Math
title: Mean — Step-Deviation Method
visual_data: \bar{x} = a + \left(\frac{\sum f_i u_i}{\sum f_i}\right) \times h, \quad u_i = \frac{x_i - a}{h}
description: Mean for equal class-width data. \(a\)=assumed mean, \(h\)=class width, \(u_i=(x_i-a)/h\), \(f_i\)=frequency.

subject: Math
title: Median (Grouped Data)
description: Median of a grouped frequency distribution. \(l\)=lower limit of median class, \(N\)=total frequency, \(C\)=cumulative frequency before median class, \(f\)=frequency of median class, \(h\)=class width.

subject: Math
title: Mode (Grouped Data)
description: Mode of a grouped distribution. \(l\)=lower limit of modal class, \(f_1\)=modal class frequency, \(f_0,f_2\)=frequencies of preceding/succeeding classes, \(h\)=class width.

subject: Math
title: Empirical Mode Relation
description: Empirical relation linking the three central tendencies for moderately skewed data. Used to find any one given the other two.

subject: Math
title: Mean Deviation about Mean
description: Average absolute deviation from the mean. \(x_i\)=values, \(\bar{x}\)=mean, \(f_i\)=frequency (use \(f_i=1\) for ungrouped).

subject: Math
title: Variance (Frequency Distribution)
description: Variance for grouped/discrete data. \(f_i\)=frequency, \(x_i\)=values, \(\bar{x}\)=mean, \(N=\sum f_i\).

subject: Math
title: Variance — Step-Deviation Form
visual_data: \sigma^2 = h^2\left[\frac{\sum f_i u_i^2}{N} - \left(\frac{\sum f_i u_i}{N}\right)^2\right], \quad u_i = \frac{x_i - a}{h}
description: Computational shortcut for variance with equal class widths. \(h\)=class width, \(a\)=assumed mean, \(u_i=(x_i-a)/h\), \(N=\sum f_i\).

subject: Math
title: Standard Deviation
description: Positive square root of variance; the standard spread measure. \(\sigma\)=SD, \(x_i\)=values, \(\bar{x}\)=mean, \(f_i\)=frequency, \(N=\sum f_i\).

subject: Math
title: Variance of First n Natural Numbers
description: Variance of \(1,2,\dots,n\) — a frequently tested standard result. \(n\)=count of natural numbers; mean \(=\frac{n+1}{2}\).

subject: Math
title: Effect of Change of Scale & Origin
visual_data: \begin{aligned} y_i &= a x_i + b \\ \bar{y} &= a\bar{x} + b \\ \sigma_y^2 &= a^2 \sigma_x^2 \end{aligned}
description: How mean and variance transform under a linear change. \(a\)=scale, \(b\)=origin shift; variance is unaffected by \(b\) and scales by \(a^2\). SD: \(\sigma_y=|a|\sigma_x\).

subject: Math
title: Root Mean Square Deviation
description: Mean square deviation about an arbitrary point \(A\); minimized when \(A=\bar{x}\), giving variance. \(\sigma^2\)=variance about mean, \(A\)=arbitrary point.

subject: Math
title: Sum of Binomial Coefficients
description: Sum of all combinatorial coefficients for power $n$.
derivation:
Binomial Expansion:
$(1+x)^n = \binom{n}{0} + \binom{n}{1}x + \binom{n}{2}x^2 + \dots + \binom{n}{n}x^n$.
Substitute $x=1$:
$(1+1)^n = \binom{n}{0} + \binom{n}{1} + \dots + \binom{n}{n}$.
$2^n = \sum \binom{n}{r}$.

related_concepts.name: Pascal's Triangle
related_concepts.definition: Triangular array where each row sums to a power of 2.

subject: Math
title: Term Independent of x
description: Finding the constant term in expansion of $(ax^p + b/x^q)^n$.
derivation:
General Term $T_{r+1} = \binom{n}{r} (ax^p)^{n-r} (bx^{-q})^r$.
Combine powers of $x$:
$x^{p(n-r)} \cdot x^{-qr} = x^{pn - pr - qr} = x^{pn - r(p+q)}$.
For term independent of x, exponent must be 0.
$pn - r(p+q) = 0 \implies r(p+q) = pn \implies r = \frac{np}{p+q}$.

related_concepts.name: Middle Term
related_concepts.definition: If $r$ from this formula is not an integer, no independent term exists.

subject: Math
title: Multinomial Theorem
description: General term in expansion of $(x_1 + x_2 + \dots + x_k)^n$.
derivation:
Combinatorial logic:
We need to arrange $n$ brackets.
We select $x_1$ from $n_1$ brackets, $x_2$ from $n_2$ brackets, etc.
Total permutations of $n$ items where $n_1$ are identical type 1, etc., is $\frac{n!}{n_1! n_2! \dots}$.

related_concepts.name: Permutations with Repetition
related_concepts.definition: Arranging objects where some are identical.

subject: Math
title: Binomial Theorem (Positive Integral Index)
description: Expansion of \((x+y)^n\) for positive integer \(n\). \(n\)=index, \(r\)=term index, \(\binom{n}{r}\)=binomial coefficient. Expansion has \(n+1\) terms; powers of \(x\) decrease, powers of \(y\) increase, exponent sum \(=n\).

subject: Math
title: General Term
description: The \((r+1)\)th term in expansion of \((x+y)^n\). \(r\) runs from \(0\) to \(n\). Used to find any specific term, coefficient, or term containing a given power.

subject: Math
title: Middle Term(s)
description: Middle term of \((x+y)^n\). If \(n\) is even there is one middle term \(T_{n/2+1}\); if \(n\) is odd there are two middle terms \(T_{(n+1)/2}\) and \(T_{(n+3)/2}\).

subject: Math
title: Numerically Greatest Term
description: Locates the numerically greatest term in \((x+y)^n\). Compute \(k=\frac{(n+1)|y/x|}{1+|y/x|}\); greatest term is \(T_{[k]+1}\) (if \(k\) non-integer) or \(T_k=T_{k+1}\) (if \(k\) integer). \([\,]\)=greatest integer.

subject: Math
title: Pascal's Rule
description: Adjacent coefficient addition rule (Pascal's triangle). Used to simplify sums of consecutive coefficients. \(0 \le r \le n\).

subject: Math
title: Coefficient Symmetry & Ratio
description: Symmetry of binomial coefficients (equidistant from ends are equal) and ratio of consecutive coefficients. Useful for greatest-coefficient and term-ratio problems.

subject: Math
title: Alternating Sum of Coefficients
description: Put \(x=-1\) in \((1+x)^n\). Implies sum of even-indexed coefficients equals sum of odd-indexed coefficients.

subject: Math
title: Sum of Even / Odd Coefficients
description: Sum of even-position coefficients equals sum of odd-position coefficients, each \(=2^{n-1}\). \(C_r=\binom{n}{r}\). Obtained by adding/subtracting \(x=1\) and \(x=-1\) substitutions.

subject: Math
title: Sum r·C_r
description: Coefficient-weighted sum, obtained by differentiating \((1+x)^n\) then putting \(x=1\). Uses \(r\binom{n}{r}=n\binom{n-1}{r-1}\).
derivation:
Differentiate \((1+x)^n=\sum \binom{n}{r}x^r\):
\(n(1+x)^{n-1}=\sum r\binom{n}{r}x^{r-1}\)
Put \(x=1\Rightarrow n\,2^{n-1}=\sum r\binom{n}{r}\)

subject: Math
title: Sum C_r / (r+1)
description: Coefficient sum with reciprocal weights, obtained by integrating \((1+x)^n\) from \(0\) to \(1\). Uses \(\frac{1}{r+1}\binom{n}{r}=\frac{1}{n+1}\binom{n+1}{r+1}\).
derivation:
\(\int_0^1 (1+x)^n dx = \frac{2^{n+1}-1}{n+1}\)
LHS \(=\int_0^1 \sum \binom{n}{r}x^r dx = \sum \frac{\binom{n}{r}}{r+1}\)

subject: Math
title: Sum of Squares of Coefficients (Vandermonde)
description: Sum of squares of all coefficients in \((1+x)^n\). Found as the coefficient of \(x^n\) in \((1+x)^n(1+x)^n=(1+x)^{2n}\).

subject: Math
title: Vandermonde's Identity
description: Product-sum of coefficients from two expansions. \(m,n,k\) non-negative integers. Comes from equating coefficient of \(x^k\) in \((1+x)^m(1+x)^n=(1+x)^{m+n}\).

subject: Math
title: Binomial Series (General Index)
description: Expansion for any real/rational \(n\), valid when \(|x|<1\). Infinite series. General term \(T_{r+1}=\frac{n(n-1)\cdots(n-r+1)}{r!}x^r\).

subject: Math
title: Standard Negative/Fractional Index Expansions
description: Memorized series for \(|x|<1\). General term: \((1-x)^{-n}\) has \(T_{r+1}=\binom{n+r-1}{r}x^r\); \((1+x)^{-n}\) has \((-1)^r\binom{n+r-1}{r}x^r\).

subject: Math
title: Number of Terms in (x+y+z)^n
description: Distinct terms in trinomial expansion \((x+y+z)^n\). General multinomial \((x_1+\cdots+x_k)^n\) has \(\binom{n+k-1}{k-1}\) terms.

subject: Math
title: Greatest Coefficient
description: The numerically greatest binomial coefficient in \((1+x)^n\). Occurs at the middle term(s). Distinct from numerically greatest term (which depends on \(x\)).

subject: Math
title: Last Digits via Binomial (Remainder)
description: Technique for remainder/last-digit problems: write base as \((1\pm k)\) and expand; terms with high powers of \(k\) are divisible. \(k\)=chosen near base, \(n\)=power.

subject: Math
title: Integral + Fractional Part Identity
description: For \(R=(p+\sqrt{q})^n\) with \(0<p-\sqrt{q}<1\): let \(I=\) integer part, \(f=\) fractional part, \(f'=(p-\sqrt q)^n\); then \(R\cdot(\text{conjugate})\) and \(I+f+f'=\) integer give \(f+f'=1\). Used to evaluate \((I+f)f\).

subject: Math
title: Contrapositive
description: A conditional statement is logically equivalent to its contrapositive.
derivation:
Using Truth Tables:
1. $p \rightarrow q$ is FALSE only when $p$ is True and $q$ is False.
2. $\sim q \rightarrow \sim p$: If $\sim q$ is True ($q$ False) and $\sim p$ is False ($p$ True), result is False.
3. In all other cases, both are True.
Therefore, truth values match exactly.

related_concepts.name: Converse
related_concepts.definition: The converse $q \rightarrow p$ is NOT equivalent to $p \rightarrow q$.

subject: Math
title: De Morgan's Laws
description: The negation of a disjunction (OR) is the conjunction (AND) of the negations.
derivation:
Logic:
To deny that 'p or q' is true, you must deny p AND deny q.
Example: 'It is not raining OR snowing' means 'It is not raining AND it is not snowing'.
Truth table verification confirms equivalence.

related_concepts.name: Set Theory Analogy
related_concepts.definition: $(A \cup B)' = A' \cap B'$.

subject: Math
title: Tautology
description: A compound statement that is always true, regardless of the truth values of its components.
derivation:
Case 1: If $p$ is True, then $(T \lor F)$ is True.
Case 2: If $p$ is False, then $(F \lor T)$ is True.
Since the result is True in all possible cases, it is a Tautology.

related_concepts.name: Law of Excluded Middle
related_concepts.definition: A proposition is either true or false; there is no third option.

subject: Math
title: Fallacy (Contradiction)
description: A statement that is always false.
derivation:
Case 1: If $p$ is True, then $(T \land F)$ is False.
Case 2: If $p$ is False, then $(F \land T)$ is False.
The AND operation requires both to be true, which is impossible here.
Thus, it is a Contradiction.

related_concepts.name: Absurdity
related_concepts.definition: Another term for a logical contradiction.

subject: Math
title: Conjunction (AND)
description: True only if both statements p and q are true.
derivation:
Truth Table Definition:
| p | q | p $\land$ q |
| T | T |  T  |
| T | F |  F  |
| F | T |  F  |
| F | F |  F  |

related_concepts.name: Intersection
related_concepts.definition: Analogous to set intersection ($A \cap B$).

subject: Math
title: Implication Equivalence
description: Equivalent form of conditional statement without arrow.
derivation:
Analyze Truth Values:
$p \rightarrow q$ is False ONLY when $p=T, q=F$.
$\sim p \lor q$ is False ONLY when $\sim p=F$ (so $p=T$) AND $q=F$.
Since the 'False' condition is identical, the statements are logically equivalent.

related_concepts.name: Conditional Statement
related_concepts.definition: If p then q.

subject: Math
title: Negation of Implication
description: Used to disprove implications (Counter-example method).
derivation:
Using equivalence $p \rightarrow q \equiv \sim p \lor q$.
$\sim(p \rightarrow q) \equiv \sim(\sim p \lor q)$.
Apply De Morgan's Law:
$\equiv \sim(\sim p) \land \sim q$
$\equiv p \land \sim q$.

related_concepts.name: Counter Example
related_concepts.definition: A case where hypothesis p is true but conclusion q is false.

subject: Math
title: Disjunction (OR)
description: True if at least one of the statements p or q is true.
derivation:
Truth Table Definition:
| p | q | p $\lor$ q |
| T | T |  T  |
| T | F |  T  |
| F | T |  T  |
| F | F |  F  |
Note: This is 'inclusive OR'.

related_concepts.name: Union
related_concepts.definition: Analogous to set union ($A \cup B$).

subject: Math
title: Biconditional (IFF)
description: True if p and q have the same truth value.
derivation:
Combines forward and backward implication.
Truth Table:
| p | q | p $\leftrightarrow$ q |
| T | T |  T  |
| T | F |  F  |
| F | T |  F  |
| F | F |  T  |
Logic: p if and only if q.

related_concepts.name: Equivalence
related_concepts.definition: Statement asserting that two propositions are logically identical.

subject: Math
title: Converse & Inverse
visual_data: \begin{aligned}\text{Converse} &: q \rightarrow p \\ \text{Inverse} &: \sim p \rightarrow \sim q \\ \text{Contrapositive} &: \sim q \rightarrow \sim p\end{aligned}
description: The three statements derived from a conditional \(p \rightarrow q\). \(p\)=hypothesis, \(q\)=conclusion. Key fact: a conditional and its contrapositive are equivalent, as are converse and inverse.

subject: Math
title: Negation of Biconditional
description: Negation of an if-and-only-if statement; equals the exclusive-OR of \(p,q\). \(p,q\)=component statements. Also written \(\sim(p\leftrightarrow q)\equiv p\leftrightarrow \sim q\).

subject: Math
title: Distributive Laws
visual_data: \begin{aligned}p \land (q \lor r) &\equiv (p \land q) \lor (p \land r) \\ p \lor (q \land r) &\equiv (p \lor q) \land (p \lor r)\end{aligned}
description: Logical connectives distribute over each other. \(p,q,r\)=statements. Mirror of set-theory distributive laws \(\cap,\cup\).

subject: Math
title: Identity & Domination Laws
visual_data: \begin{aligned}p \land T &\equiv p, \quad p \lor F \equiv p \\ p \lor T &\equiv T, \quad p \land F \equiv F\end{aligned}
description: Behaviour of statements with tautology \(T\) and contradiction \(F\). \(p\)=any statement. \(T\)=always true, \(F\)=always false.

subject: Math
title: Idempotent & Double Negation
visual_data: p \land p \equiv p, \quad p \lor p \equiv p, \quad \sim(\sim p) \equiv p
description: Repetition collapses; negating twice restores the statement. \(p\)=any statement.

subject: Math
title: Complement (Negation) Laws
visual_data: p \lor \sim p \equiv T, \quad p \land \sim p \equiv F, \quad \sim T \equiv F
description: A statement with its own negation; and negation of constants. \(p\)=statement, \(T\)=true, \(F\)=false. Foundation of tautology and contradiction.

subject: Math
title: De Morgan's Law (AND form)
description: Negation of a conjunction becomes disjunction of negations. \(p,q\)=statements. Companion to the OR-form De Morgan law.

subject: Math
title: Negation of Quantifiers
visual_data: \begin{aligned}\sim(\forall x,\ p(x)) &\equiv \exists x,\ \sim p(x) \\ \sim(\exists x,\ p(x)) &\equiv \forall x,\ \sim p(x)\end{aligned}
description: Negating universal/existential quantified statements swaps the quantifier and negates the predicate. \(\forall\)=for all, \(\exists\)=there exists, \(p(x)\)=open statement.

subject: Math
title: Truth Value Counts
description: Number of distinct true/false combinations (rows) for \(n\) simple statements. \(n\)=number of atomic statements. Each connective column is then filled per its rule.

subject: Math
title: Conditional Identities
visual_data: \begin{aligned}p \rightarrow q &\equiv \sim q \rightarrow \sim p \\ p \leftrightarrow q &\equiv (p \rightarrow q) \land (q \rightarrow p) \\ p \leftrightarrow q &\equiv (p \land q) \lor (\sim p \land \sim q)\end{aligned}
description: Useful rewrites for implication and biconditional. \(p,q\)=statements. The last line gives the biconditional as agreement of truth values.

subject: Math
title: Absorption Laws
visual_data: p \lor (p \land q) \equiv p, \quad p \land (p \lor q) \equiv p
description: A statement absorbs the connective it appears in. \(p,q\)=statements. Used to simplify compound expressions.

subject: Math
title: Commutative & Associative Laws
visual_data: \begin{aligned}p \land q &\equiv q \land p, \quad p \lor q \equiv q \lor p \\ (p \land q)\land r &\equiv p \land (q \land r)\end{aligned}
description: Order and grouping of \(\land,\lor\) do not affect truth value. \(p,q,r\)=statements. (\(\lor\) is associative identically.)

subject: Math
title: Slope of Tangent
description: Geometric interpretation of the derivative at a point.
derivation:
Consider a curve $y = f(x)$.
Consider a secant line passing through $P(x, f(x))$ and $Q(x+h, f(x+h))$.
Slope of secant = $\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}$.
As $Q \to P$ ($h \to 0$), the secant becomes the tangent.
$m_T = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} = \frac{dy}{dx}$.

related_concepts.name: Inclination
related_concepts.definition: Angle $\psi$ made by the tangent with the positive x-axis.

subject: Math
title: Slope of Normal
description: Slope of the line perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact.
derivation:
Condition for perpendicular lines: $m_1 m_2 = -1$.
Since Normal $\perp$ Tangent:
$m_N \times m_T = -1$
$m_N = -\frac{1}{m_T} = -\frac{1}{dy/dx} = -\frac{dx}{dy}$.

subject: Math
title: Increasing Function Condition
description: Function value increases or stays constant as x increases.
derivation:
Let $x_2 > x_1$. For increasing, $f(x_2) \ge f(x_1)$.
Using Mean Value Theorem: $\frac{f(x_2) - f(x_1)}{x_2 - x_1} = f'(c)$.
Since denominator is positive, numerator is positive only if $f'(c) \ge 0$.
Strictly Increasing if $f'(x) > 0$.

related_concepts.name: Monotonicity
related_concepts.definition: Behavior of a function being purely increasing or decreasing.

subject: Math
title: Decreasing Function Condition
description: Function value decreases as x increases.
derivation:
Let $x_2 > x_1$. For decreasing, $f(x_2) \le f(x_1)$.
Change $\Delta y = f(x_2) - f(x_1) \le 0$.
Change $\Delta x = x_2 - x_1 > 0$.
Ratio $\frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} \le 0$.
Limit as $\Delta x \to 0$ implies $f'(x) \le 0$.

related_concepts.name: Critical Point
related_concepts.definition: Point where nature changes, often where $f'(x)=0$.

subject: Math
title: Rate Measure
description: Relating rates of change of two variables using Chain Rule.
derivation:
Given $y$ is a function of $x$, and both change with time $t$.
Differentiate $y = f(x)$ with respect to $t$:
$\frac{d}{dt}(y) = \frac{d}{dt}(f(x))$
Using Chain Rule:
$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{df}{dx} \times \frac{dx}{dt}$.

related_concepts.name: Related Rates
related_concepts.definition: Problems where rate of one quantity determines rate of another (e.g., radius vs area).

subject: Math
title: Angle of Intersection
description: The acute angle between the tangents of two curves at their intersection point.
derivation:
1. Find intersection point $(x_1, y_1)$ by solving equations.
2. Find slopes $m_1 = f'(x_1)$ and $m_2 = g'(x_1)$ at that point.
3. Angle between lines formula:
   $\tan \theta = \tan (\psi_1 - \psi_2) = \frac{\tan \psi_1 - \tan \psi_2}{1 + \tan \psi_1 \tan \psi_2}$.

related_concepts.name: Orthogonal Curves
related_concepts.definition: Curves intersecting at $90^\circ$ ($m_1 m_2 = -1$).

subject: Math
title: Approximation by Differentials
description: Using tangent line to estimate function value near a point.
derivation:
Definition of derivative: $f'(x) = \lim_{\Delta x \to 0} \frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}$.
For small $\Delta x$: $\frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} \approx f'(x)$.
$\Delta y \approx f'(x) \Delta x$.
Since $y_{new} = y + \Delta y$:
$f(x + \Delta x) \approx f(x) + f'(x)\Delta x$.

related_concepts.name: Linearization
related_concepts.definition: Approximating a curve by a line $L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x-a)$.

subject: Math
title: Subtangent Length
description: The projection of the tangent segment on the x-axis.
derivation:
Consider point $P(x,y)$ on curve.
Tangent meets x-axis at $T$. Draw perpendicular $PM$ to x-axis.
In $\Delta PTM$, slope $\tan \psi = \frac{PM}{TM} = \frac{y}{ST}$.
Rearrange: $ST = y / \tan \psi = y / m = y / (dy/dx)$.

related_concepts.name: Tangent Length
related_concepts.definition: Length of segment PT: $|y| \sqrt{1 + (1/m)^2}$.

subject: Math
title: Subnormal Length
description: The projection of the normal segment on the x-axis.
derivation:
Consider point $P(x,y)$. Normal meets x-axis at $N$. $PM$ is perpendicular to x-axis.
In $\Delta PMN$, angle at $P$ is $\psi$ (since Normal $\perp$ Tangent).
Slope $\tan \psi = \frac{MN}{PM} = \frac{SN}{y}$.
Rearrange: $SN = y \tan \psi = y (dy/dx)$.

related_concepts.name: Constant Subnormal
related_concepts.definition: Property of the parabola $y^2 = 4ax$ ($SN = 2a$).

subject: Math
title: Critical Point
description: Interior points in the domain where extrema can occur.
derivation:
Fermat's Theorem: If local extremum exists at $c$ and $f$ is differentiable, then $f'(c) = 0$.
However, peaks (cusps) can also be extrema where derivative is undefined.
Therefore, Critical Points include:
1. Stationary points ($f' = 0$).
2. Points of non-differentiability.

related_concepts.name: Inflection Point
related_concepts.definition: Point where concavity changes (requires $f''$ test).

subject: Math
title: Second Derivative Test
description: Test for local extrema at critical point $c$ where $f'(c)=0$.
derivation:
1. If $f''(c) < 0$, the graph is Concave Down (frowning).
   A flat tangent ($f'=0$) on a frown must be a peak (Maxima).
2. If $f''(c) > 0$, the graph is Concave Up (smiling).
   A flat tangent on a smile must be a bottom (Minima).

related_concepts.name: Concavity
related_concepts.definition: Direction of curvature. $f'' > 0$ is convex (up), $f'' < 0$ is concave (down).

subject: Math
title: Equation of Tangent
description: Line touching the curve at a point. \((x_1, y_1)\)=point of contact, \(\frac{dy}{dx}\)=slope at that point.

subject: Math
title: Equation of Normal
description: Line perpendicular to tangent at point of contact. \((x_1, y_1)\)=point, \(\frac{dy}{dx}\)=slope of tangent there.

subject: Math
title: Horizontal / Vertical Tangent
description: Conditions for tangent parallel to axes. Horizontal tangent when slope \(=0\); vertical when slope \(\to \infty\).

subject: Math
title: Length of Tangent
description: Distance from point of contact to where tangent meets x-axis. \(y\)=ordinate, \(\frac{dy}{dx}\)=slope.

subject: Math
title: Length of Normal
description: Distance from point of contact to where normal meets x-axis. \(y\)=ordinate, \(\frac{dy}{dx}\)=slope of tangent.

subject: Math
title: Tangent for Parametric Curve
description: Slope when curve is given parametrically as \(x=f(t), y=g(t)\). \(t\)=parameter.

subject: Math
title: Strictly Increasing / Decreasing
description: Strict monotonicity on an interval. \(f'(x)\)=derivative; strict inequality on the whole interval.

subject: Math
title: First Derivative Test
description: Sign change of \(f'\) across critical point \(c\) classifies extremum. No sign change \(\Rightarrow\) point of inflexion.

subject: Math
title: Higher Order Derivative Test
description: When second-derivative test fails. If \(n\) even: extremum (min if \(f^{(n)}(c)>0\), max if \(<0\)); if \(n\) odd: inflexion.

subject: Math
title: Point of Inflexion
visual_data: f''(c) = 0 \text{ and } f'' \text{ changes sign at } c
description: Where concavity reverses. \(f''>0\)=concave up, \(f''<0\)=concave down; \(c\) separates the two.

subject: Math
title: Absolute Extrema on [a,b]
description: Global max/min of continuous \(f\) on closed interval. \(c_i\)=critical points in \((a,b)\); also check endpoints \(a,b\).

subject: Math
title: Rolle's Theorem
description: For \(f\) continuous on \([a,b]\), differentiable on \((a,b)\). Guarantees a stationary point \(c\) inside.

subject: Math
title: Lagrange Mean Value Theorem
description: Some tangent is parallel to the chord. \(f\) continuous on \([a,b]\), differentiable on \((a,b)\).

subject: Math
title: Percentage Error / Approximation
description: Relative/percentage error via differentials. \(\Delta x\)=error in \(x\), \(dy\)=approx change, \(\frac{dy}{y}\)=relative error.

subject: Math
title: Marginal Cost / Revenue
description: Instantaneous rate of cost/revenue per unit output. \(C\)=total cost, \(R\)=total revenue, \(x\)=units produced.

subject: Math
title: Tangent from Origin Condition
description: Curve's tangent passes through origin: slope equals \(y_1/x_1\). \((x_1,y_1)\)=point of contact on the curve.

subject: Math
title: Orthogonal Curves Condition
description: Two curves cut at right angles at the intersection point. \(m_1, m_2\)=slopes of the two curves there.

subject: Math
title: AM-GM for Extrema
description: Quick max/min of products/sums (equality when all equal). \(a_i > 0\); used to bound optimization expressions.

subject: Math
title: Sine Rule
description: Relates sides to opposite angles and circumradius $R$.
derivation:
In $\Delta ABC$, draw circumcircle with center $O$.
Draw diameter $BD$. Connect $C$ to $D$.
Angle $BCD = 90^\circ$ (Angle in semi-circle).
Angle $BDC = A$ (Angles in same segment).
In $\Delta BCD$: $\sin D = \frac{BC}{BD} \implies \sin A = \frac{a}{2R}$.
Thus, $\frac{a}{\sin A} = 2R$.

related_concepts.name: Triangle Area
related_concepts.definition: Area $= \frac{abc}{4R} = 2R^2 \sin A \sin B \sin C$.

subject: Math
title: Cosine Rule
description: Generalized Pythagorean theorem for any triangle.
derivation:
Vector Method:
$\vec{BC} = \vec{AC} - \vec{AB} \implies \vec{a} = \vec{b} - \vec{c}$.
Square magnitudes:
$|\vec{a}|^2 = |\vec{b} - \vec{c}|^2$
$a^2 = |\vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{c}|^2 - 2 \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}$
$a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc \cos A$.

related_concepts.name: Obtuse Triangle
related_concepts.definition: If $\cos A < 0$ ($A > 90^\circ$), then $a^2 > b^2 + c^2$.

subject: Math
title: Projection Formula
description: Expresses a side as the sum of projections of the other two sides.
derivation:
Draw altitude $AD$ perpendicular to $BC$.
$D$ divides $BC$ into $BD$ and $DC$.
In right $\Delta ABD$: $BD = c \cos B$.
In right $\Delta ACD$: $DC = b \cos C$.
$a = BC = BD + DC = c \cos B + b \cos C$.

related_concepts.name: Vector Projection
related_concepts.definition: Geometric equivalent using dot product components.

subject: Math
title: Napier's Analogy
description: Tangent rule useful for solving triangles given two sides and included angle.
derivation:
From Sine Rule: $b = k \sin B, c = k \sin C$.
$\frac{b-c}{b+c} = \frac{\sin B - \sin C}{\sin B + \sin C}$.
Apply Sum-to-Product formulas:
$= \frac{2 \cos \frac{B+C}{2} \sin \frac{B-C}{2}}{2 \sin \frac{B+C}{2} \cos \frac{B-C}{2}} = \cot \frac{B+C}{2} \tan \frac{B-C}{2}$.
Since $\frac{B+C}{2} = 90 - A/2$, $\cot(90-A/2) = \tan(A/2)$.
Rearranging gives the formula.

related_concepts.name: Law of Tangents
related_concepts.definition: Another name for Napier's Analogy.

subject: Math
title: Heron's Formula
description: Area of triangle given sides $a, b, c$ and semi-perimeter $s$.
derivation:
Start with $\Delta = \frac{1}{2}bc \sin A$.
$\sin A = \sqrt{1 - \cos^2 A}$. Use Cosine Rule for $\cos A = \frac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2bc}$.
$\Delta = \frac{1}{2}bc \sqrt{1 - (\frac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2bc})^2}$.
$\Delta = \frac{1}{4} \sqrt{4b^2c^2 - (b^2+c^2-a^2)^2}$.
Factor using difference of squares $(2bc - b^2 - c^2 + a^2)...$
Substitute $2s = a+b+c$ to simplify to the final form.

subject: Math
title: Inradius (r)
description: Radius of the circle tangent to all three sides internally.
derivation:
Connect Incenter $I$ to vertices A, B, C.
Area $\Delta = Area(\Delta IAB) + Area(\Delta IBC) + Area(\Delta ICA)$.
Height of each small triangle is $r$.
$\Delta = \frac{1}{2} c \cdot r + \frac{1}{2} a \cdot r + \frac{1}{2} b \cdot r$.
$\Delta = r \left( \frac{a+b+c}{2} \right) = r \cdot s$.

related_concepts.name: Trig Form
related_concepts.definition: $r = (s-a) \tan(A/2) = 4R \sin(A/2) \sin(B/2) \sin(C/2)$.

subject: Math
title: Inradius (r)
description: Radius of the inscribed circle tangent to all three sides.
derivation:
Area Summation Method:
Connect Incenter $I$ to vertices A, B, C.
Area $\Delta = \text{Ar}(\Delta IAB) + \text{Ar}(\Delta IBC) + \text{Ar}(\Delta ICA)$.
$\Delta = \frac{1}{2}c r + \frac{1}{2}a r + \frac{1}{2}b r$.
$\Delta = r \left(\frac{a+b+c}{2}\right) = r s$.
Trig form derived using Sine Rule $a=2R\sin A$ and half-angle formulas.

subject: Math
title: Circumradius (R)
description: Radius of the circle passing through all three vertices.
derivation:
Area of triangle $\Delta = \frac{1}{2} bc \sin A$.
From Sine Rule: $\sin A = \frac{a}{2R}$.
Substitute $\sin A$ into Area formula:
$\Delta = \frac{1}{2} bc \left( \frac{a}{2R} \right) = \frac{abc}{4R}$.
Rearrange: $R = \frac{abc}{4\Delta}$.

related_concepts.name: Sine Rule
related_concepts.definition: $a/\sin A = b/\sin B = c/\sin C = 2R$.

subject: Math
title: Ex-radii
description: Radius of escribed circle opposite to vertex A.
derivation:
Let $I_1$ be the excenter opposite A.
$\Delta = \text{Ar}(ABI_1) + \text{Ar}(ACI_1) - \text{Ar}(BCI_1)$.
$\Delta = \frac{1}{2}c r_1 + \frac{1}{2}b r_1 - \frac{1}{2}a r_1$.
$\Delta = r_1 \frac{b+c-a}{2} = r_1 \frac{2s-2a}{2} = r_1(s-a)$.

related_concepts.name: Excenters
related_concepts.definition: Points where one internal and two external angle bisectors intersect.

subject: Math
title: Length of Median (Apollonius)
description: Length of median from vertex A to side a.
derivation:
Apply Apollonius Theorem to $\Delta ABC$ with median $AD$:
$AB^2 + AC^2 = 2(AD^2 + BD^2)$.
$c^2 + b^2 = 2(m_a^2 + (a/2)^2)$.
$b^2 + c^2 = 2m_a^2 + a^2/2$.
$2m_a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - a^2/2$. Multiply by 2 and solve.

related_concepts.name: Centroid
related_concepts.definition: Point dividing median in 2:1 ratio.

subject: Math
title: Orthocenter Distance (OH)
description: Distance between Circumcenter (O) and Orthocenter (H).
derivation:
Using vector method with origin at O:
$\vec{H} = \vec{A} + \vec{B} + \vec{C}$.
$OH^2 = |\vec{A} + \vec{B} + \vec{C}|^2 = R^2 + R^2 + R^2 + 2R^2(\cos 2A + \cos 2B + \cos 2C)$.
Substitute identity: $\cos 2A + \cos 2B + \cos 2C = -1 - 4\cos A \cos B \cos C$.
$OH^2 = 3R^2 + 2R^2(-1 - 4\Pi \cos A) = R^2(1 - 8\Pi \cos A)$.

related_concepts.name: Euler Line
related_concepts.definition: Line passing through H, G, O. $HG:GO = 2:1$.

subject: Math
title: Incenter Distance (Euler's Theorem)
description: Distance between Circumcenter and Incenter.
derivation:
Standard geometric proof involving power of a point:
Let line $AI$ cut circumcircle at $L$.
$R^2 - d^2 = AI \cdot IL$.
Substitute $AI = r/\sin(A/2)$ and $IL = 2R \sin(A/2)$.
$R^2 - d^2 = 2Rr \implies d^2 = R^2 - 2Rr$.

related_concepts.name: Euler's Inequality
related_concepts.definition: $R \ge 2r$ (Equality holds for equilateral triangle).

subject: Math
title: Half-Angle (sin)
description: Half-angle sine in terms of sides; key for proving identities. \(s\)=semi-perimeter, \(a,b,c\)=sides opposite \(A,B,C\).

subject: Math
title: Half-Angle (cos)
description: Half-angle cosine in terms of sides. \(s\)=semi-perimeter, \(a,b,c\)=sides opposite \(A,B,C\).

subject: Math
title: Half-Angle (tan)
description: Half-angle tangent in terms of sides/area. \(s\)=semi-perimeter, \(\Delta\)=area, \(a,b,c\)=sides.

subject: Math
title: Area (Two Sides & Angle)
visual_data: \Delta = \frac{1}{2} ab \sin C = \frac{1}{2} bc \sin A = \frac{1}{2} ca \sin B
description: Triangle area from two sides and included angle. \(\Delta\)=area, \(a,b,c\)=sides, \(A,B,C\)=angles.

subject: Math
title: Area (Sine Form)
description: Area via circumradius and angles. \(\Delta\)=area, \(R\)=circumradius, \(A,B,C\)=angles, \(a,b,c\)=sides.

subject: Math
title: Area = rs
description: Area linking in-radius and ex-radii. \(\Delta\)=area, \(r\)=inradius, \(r_1,r_2,r_3\)=ex-radii, \(s\)=semi-perimeter.

subject: Math
title: Mollweide's Formulas
description: Relate side sums/differences to angles (checks Napier's analogy). \(a,b,c\)=sides, \(A,B,C\)=angles.

subject: Math
title: Sum of Two Inradii Relations
description: Standard ex-radii identity (frequently tested). \(r_1,r_2,r_3\)=ex-radii, \(r\)=inradius, \(R\)=circumradius.

subject: Math
title: Ex-radius Trig Form
description: Ex-radius opposite \(A\) via circumradius and half-angles. \(r_1\)=ex-radius, \(R\)=circumradius, \(A,B,C\)=angles.

subject: Math
title: Inradius Reciprocal Identity
description: Reciprocal in-radius / ex-radii identity. \(r\)=inradius, \(r_1,r_2,r_3\)=ex-radii.

subject: Math
title: Ex-radii Pairwise Sum
description: Symmetric ex-radii relation. \(r_1,r_2,r_3\)=ex-radii, \(s\)=semi-perimeter.

subject: Math
title: Tangent Rule (Tan of Half-Sum)
visual_data: \tan A + \tan B + \tan C = \tan A \tan B \tan C
description: Holds since \(A+B+C=\pi\); used in triangle angle problems. \(A,B,C\)=angles.

subject: Math
title: Cotangent Half-Angle Sum
description: Half-angle cotangent identity for triangle. \(A,B,C\)=angles with \(A+B+C=\pi\).

subject: Math
title: Sum of cos = 1 + r/R
description: Links angle-cosine sum to in/circum-radii. \(A,B,C\)=angles, \(r\)=inradius, \(R\)=circumradius.

subject: Math
title: Product of cos
visual_data: \cos A \cos B + \cos B \cos C + \cos C \cos A = \frac{s^2 + r^2 - 4R^2}{4R^2}
description: Symmetric cosine-product identity. \(s\)=semi-perimeter, \(r\)=inradius, \(R\)=circumradius.

subject: Math
title: Sum of sin
description: Angle-sine sum identity. \(s\)=semi-perimeter, \(R\)=circumradius, \(A,B,C\)=angles.

subject: Math
title: Sum of sin 2A
description: Double-angle sine sum for triangle. \(A,B,C\)=angles with \(A+B+C=\pi\).

subject: Math
title: Sum of cos 2A
description: Double-angle cosine sum for triangle. \(A,B,C\)=angles with \(A+B+C=\pi\).

subject: Math
title: Cotangent in terms of Area
description: Angle cotangent via sides and area (from cosine rule). \(\Delta\)=area, \(a,b,c\)=sides.

subject: Math
title: m-n Theorem
visual_data: (m+n) \cot \theta = m \cot \alpha - n \cot \beta = n \cot B - m \cot C
description: Cevian dividing base in ratio \(m:n\). \(\theta\)=cevian-base angle, \(\alpha,\beta\)=segment angles at apex, \(B,C\)=base angles.

subject: Math
title: Length of Angle Bisector
description: Internal bisector length from vertex \(A\) to side \(a\). \(t_a\)=bisector length, \(b,c\)=adjacent sides, \(A\)=angle.

subject: Math
title: Distance: Circumcenter to Side
description: Perpendicular distance from circumcenter \(O\) to side \(a\). \(R\)=circumradius, \(A\)=angle opposite that side.

subject: Math
title: Distance: Vertex to Orthocenter
description: Distance from vertex \(A\) to orthocenter \(H\). \(R\)=circumradius, \(A\)=angle at that vertex.

subject: Math
title: Distance: Orthocenter to Side
