subject: Math
title: Pedal Triangle Sides
visual_data: a' = a \cos A, \quad b' = b \cos B, \quad c' = c \cos C
description: Sides of pedal (orthic) triangle of an acute triangle. \(a',b',c'\)=pedal sides, \(A,B,C\)=original angles.

subject: Math
title: Pedal Triangle Angles
description: Angles of the pedal (orthic) triangle. \(A,B,C\)=angles of original acute triangle.

subject: Math
title: Area of Cyclic Quadrilateral
description: Brahmagupta's formula for a cyclic quadrilateral. \(\Delta\)=area, \(a,b,c,d\)=sides, \(s\)=semi-perimeter.

subject: Math
title: Ptolemy's Theorem
visual_data: AC \cdot BD = AB \cdot CD + BC \cdot AD
description: For a cyclic quadrilateral, product of diagonals equals sum of products of opposite sides.

subject: Math
title: Area of Regular Polygon
description: Area of an \(n\)-sided regular polygon. \(n\)=sides, \(a\)=side length, \(R\)=circumradius.

subject: Math
title: Regular Polygon: In/Circum Radius
description: Circum- and in-radius of a regular \(n\)-gon of side \(a\). \(n\)=number of sides.

subject: Math
title: Angle of Elevation/Depression
description: Basic heights-and-distances relation. \(\theta\)=angle of elevation/depression, \(h\)=height, \(d\)=horizontal distance.

subject: Math
title: Height: Two Angles (Same Side)
description: Tower height when observed from two points distance \(d\) apart on the same side. \(\alpha,\beta\)=elevations (\(\beta>\alpha\)).

subject: Math
title: Height: Two Angles (Opposite Sides)
description: Object height when foot lies between two observation points \(d\) apart. \(\alpha,\beta\)=elevations from the two ends.

subject: Math
title: Sin 3A Identity
description: Expansion of sine of triple angle.
derivation:
Use sum formula: $\sin(2A + A)$.
$= \sin 2A \cos A + \cos 2A \sin A$
$= (2\sin A \cos A)\cos A + (1 - 2\sin^2 A)\sin A$
$= 2\sin A (1-\sin^2 A) + \sin A - 2\sin^3 A$
$= 2\sin A - 2\sin^3 A + \sin A - 2\sin^3 A$
$= 3\sin A - 4\sin^3 A$.

related_concepts.name: Triple Angle
related_concepts.definition: Identity useful for integrating $\sin^3 x$.

subject: Math
title: Cos 3A Identity
description: Expansion of cosine of triple angle.
derivation:
Use $\cos(2A + A) = \cos 2A \cos A - \sin 2A \sin A$.
$= (2\cos^2 A - 1)\cos A - (2\sin A \cos A)\sin A$
$= 2\cos^3 A - \cos A - 2\cos A (1-\cos^2 A)$
$= 2\cos^3 A - \cos A - 2\cos A + 2\cos^3 A$
$= 4\cos^3 A - 3\cos A$.

subject: Math
title: Tan 3A Identity
description: Expansion of tangent of triple angle.
derivation:
$\tan(2A+A) = \frac{\tan 2A + \tan A}{1 - \tan 2A \tan A}$.
Substitute $\tan 2A = \frac{2\tan A}{1-\tan^2 A}$.
Numerator: $\frac{2\tan A}{1-\tan^2 A} + \tan A = \frac{3\tan A - \tan^3 A}{1-\tan^2 A}$.
Denominator: $1 - \frac{2\tan^2 A}{1-\tan^2 A} = \frac{1-3\tan^2 A}{1-\tan^2 A}$.
Cancel denominators.

related_concepts.name: Tan Sum Formula
related_concepts.definition: $\tan(A+B) = \frac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A \tan B}$.

subject: Math
title: Sum to Product (Sine)
description: Converts sum of sines into a product.
derivation:
Let $A = (C+D)/2$ and $B = (C-D)/2$.
Then $C = A+B$ and $D = A-B$.
$\sin(A+B) + \sin(A-B) = (\sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B) + (\sin A \cos B - \cos A \sin B)$.
$= 2\sin A \cos B$.
Substitute back A and B.

related_concepts.name: Factorization Formula
related_concepts.definition: Another name for Sum-to-Product formulas.

subject: Math
title: Product to Sum (Sine-Cos)
description: Converts product into sum. Essential for integration.
derivation:
Add expansion formulas:
$\sin(A+B) = \sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B$
$\sin(A-B) = \sin A \cos B - \cos A \sin B$
Sum = $2\sin A \cos B$.

related_concepts.name: De-factorization
related_concepts.definition: Process of converting products to sums/differences.

subject: Math
title: General Solution (Sine)
description: Solution for $\sin \theta = \sin \alpha$, where $\alpha \in [-\pi/2, \pi/2]$.
derivation:
$\sin \theta - \sin \alpha = 0$.
$2 \sin\frac{\theta-\alpha}{2} \cos\frac{\theta+\alpha}{2} = 0$.
Case 1: $\frac{\theta-\alpha}{2} = k\pi \implies \theta = 2k\pi + \alpha$ (Even multiples of $\pi$).
Case 2: $\frac{\theta+\alpha}{2} = (2k+1)\frac{\pi}{2} \implies \theta = (2k+1)\pi - \alpha$ (Odd multiples).
Combine: $n\pi + (-1)^n \alpha$.

related_concepts.name: Principal Solution
related_concepts.definition: The smallest numerical value of angle satisfying the equation.

subject: Math
title: General Solution (Cosine)
description: Solution for $\cos \theta = \cos \alpha$, where $\alpha \in [0, \pi]$.
derivation:
$\cos \theta - \cos \alpha = 0$.
$-2 \sin\frac{\theta+\alpha}{2} \sin\frac{\theta-\alpha}{2} = 0$.
$\frac{\theta \pm \alpha}{2} = n\pi$.
$\theta \pm \alpha = 2n\pi$.
$\theta = 2n\pi \mp \alpha$ (Combined as $\pm$).

related_concepts.name: Periodicity
related_concepts.definition: Cosine repeats every $2\pi$.

subject: Math
title: General Solution (Tangent)
description: Solution for $\tan \theta = \tan \alpha$, where $\alpha \in (-\pi/2, \pi/2)$.
derivation:
$\tan \theta - \tan \alpha = 0$.
$\frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} - \frac{\sin \alpha}{\cos \alpha} = 0$.
$\frac{\sin \theta \cos \alpha - \cos \theta \sin \alpha}{\cos \theta \cos \alpha} = 0$.
$\sin(\theta - \alpha) = 0$ (assuming $\cos$ terms $\neq 0$).
$\theta - \alpha = n\pi \implies \theta = n\pi + \alpha$.

related_concepts.name: Asymptotes
related_concepts.definition: Tangent is undefined at odd multiples of $\pi/2$.

subject: Math
title: Max/Min of aSin + bCos
description: Range of linear combination of sine and cosine.
derivation:
Let $a = r \cos \phi$ and $b = r \sin \phi$.
Then $r = \sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.
Expression becomes $r(\cos \phi \sin x + \sin \phi \cos x) = r \sin(x+\phi)$.
Since $-1 \le \sin(x+\phi) \le 1$:
$-r \le \text{Expression} \le r$.

related_concepts.name: Amplitude
related_concepts.definition: The magnitude of oscillation $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.

subject: Math
title: m-n Theorem
description: Relates segments of the base of a triangle to the angles.
derivation:
In $\Delta ABC$, point D divides BC in ratio $m:n$. $\theta = \angle ADC$.
Apply Sine Rule in $\Delta ABD$ and $\Delta ACD$.
$m/\sin B = AD/\sin(\theta-\alpha)$ and $n/\sin C = AD/\sin(180-\theta-\beta)$.
Divide equations and expand sin terms to derive the relation.

related_concepts.name: Appollonius Theorem
related_concepts.definition: Can be derived as a special case where $m=n$ (Median).

subject: Math
title: Pythagorean Identities
description: Fundamental relations among trig ratios. \(\theta\)=angle; valid wherever functions are defined.

subject: Math
title: Sin(A+B) / Sin(A-B)
description: Compound angle formula for sine. \(A, B\)=any angles.

subject: Math
title: Cos(A+B) / Cos(A-B)
description: Compound angle formula for cosine. \(A, B\)=any angles (note sign flips).

subject: Math
title: Tan(A+B) / Tan(A-B)
description: Compound angle formula for tangent. \(A, B\)=angles with \(\tan\) defined.

subject: Math
title: Sin 2A Identity
description: Double angle for sine, with tangent form. \(A\)=angle.

subject: Math
title: Cos 2A Identity
visual_data: \cos 2A = \cos^2 A - \sin^2 A = 2\cos^2 A - 1 = 1 - 2\sin^2 A = \frac{1 - \tan^2 A}{1 + \tan^2 A}
description: Double angle for cosine, all four standard forms. \(A\)=angle.

subject: Math
title: Tan 2A Identity
description: Double angle for tangent. \(A\)=angle with \(\tan A\) defined, \(\tan^2 A \ne 1\).

subject: Math
title: Half-Angle (Power Reduction)
description: Express squares via double angle; key for integration & simplification. \(A\)=angle.

subject: Math
title: Sum to Product (Cosine)
description: Converts sum of cosines to product. \(C, D\)=angles.

subject: Math
title: Difference to Product (Cosine)
description: Converts difference of cosines to product (note minus sign). \(C, D\)=angles.

subject: Math
title: Product to Sum (Cosines)
description: Converts products of cosines/sines to sums. \(A, B\)=angles.

subject: Math
title: Half-Angle in Terms of tan(A/2)
description: Weierstrass substitution; express all ratios via \(t=\tan(A/2)\). \(A\)=angle.

subject: Math
title: Triple Product Identity
visual_data: 4\sin A \sin(60^\circ - A) \sin(60^\circ + A) = \sin 3A \\ 4\cos A \cos(60^\circ - A) \cos(60^\circ + A) = \cos 3A
description: Factorised triple-angle results; also \(\tan A\tan(60-A)\tan(60+A)=\tan 3A\). \(A\)=angle.

subject: Math
title: Sum of Sines in AP
description: Sum of \(n\) sines whose angles are in AP. \(\alpha\)=first angle, \(\beta\)=common difference, \(n\)=count.

subject: Math
title: Conditional: A+B+C = pi
visual_data: \tan A + \tan B + \tan C = \tan A \tan B \tan C \\ \cot A \cot B + \cot B \cot C + \cot C \cot A = 1
description: Identities when angles of a triangle sum to \(\pi\). \(A+B+C=\pi\).

subject: Math
title: Conditional: Half-Angle Sum (A+B+C=pi)
description: Half-angle identities for a triangle. \(A+B+C=\pi\).

subject: Math
title: Conditional: Sin/Cos Sums (A+B+C=pi)
visual_data: \sin 2A + \sin 2B + \sin 2C = 4\sin A \sin B \sin C \\ \cos 2A + \cos 2B + \cos 2C = -1 - 4\cos A \cos B \cos C
description: Standard triangle sum identities. \(A+B+C=\pi\).

subject: Math
title: Range of sec & cosec
description: Bounds on the basic trig functions. \(\theta\)=angle; \(\sec,\csc\) never lie in \((-1,1)\).

subject: Math
title: Cos 15 / Sin 15
description: Standard exact values for \(15^\circ\) and \(75^\circ\). Also \(\tan 15^\circ = 2 - \sqrt 3\).

subject: Math
title: Sin 18 / Cos 36
description: Exact values at \(18^\circ, 36^\circ\) (golden-ratio angles). Frequently tested.

subject: Math
title: Sign & Quarter (ASTC)
description: ASTC rule for signs of ratios by quadrant. Used in solving equations & reduction.

subject: Math
title: General Solution: cos=0, sin=0
description: Boundary-case general solutions. \(n\in\mathbb{Z}\).

subject: Math
title: a sin x + b cos x as R sin
visual_data: a\sin x + b\cos x = R\sin(x + \phi), \quad R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}, \quad \tan\phi = \frac{b}{a}
description: Single-sinusoid form used for max/min and solving. \(a,b\)=coefficients, \(R\)=amplitude, \(\phi\)=phase.

subject: Math
title: Product cos(A)cos(2A)...
description: Product of cosines with doubling angles. \(n\)=number of factors, \(\sin A \ne 0\).
derivation:
Multiply and divide by \(2\sin A\).
Use \(2\sin A\cos A=\sin 2A\) repeatedly (telescoping).
Each step doubles the angle, leaving \(\sin 2^n A\) over \(2^n\sin A\).

subject: Math
title: Allied / Reduction Angles
description: Convert allied angles to base angle. \(\theta\)=acute reference; odd multiple of \(90^\circ\) flips co-function.

subject: Math
title: Range of a sin^2 + b cos^2
description: Bounds for a convex combination of \(\sin^2,\cos^2\). \(a,b\)=constants; equals \(a\) or \(b\) at axis points.

subject: Math
title: Area of Triangle
visual_data: \Delta = \frac{1}{2} \left| \det \begin{pmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \right|
description: Absolute value of determinant gives area. If 0, points are collinear.
derivation:
From coordinate geometry formula:
Area $= \frac{1}{2} |x_1(y_2-y_3) + x_2(y_3-y_1) + x_3(y_1-y_2)|$.
Expanding the determinant along Column 1:
$x_1(y_2(1)-1(y_3)) - x_2(y_1(1)-1(y_3)) + x_3(y_1(1)-1(y_2))$.
This expansion matches the coordinate formula exactly.

related_concepts.name: Collinearity Condition
related_concepts.definition: Area = 0 implies the three points lie on a straight line.

subject: Math
title: Cramer's Rule (Unique Solution)
visual_data: D \neq 0 \implies x = D_x/D, y = D_y/D, z = D_z/D
description: Method to solve linear equations using determinants.
derivation:
System $AX = B$.
$x = \frac{|A_x|}{|A|}$ where $A_x$ replaces the x-column with constants vector B.
Geometric interpretation involving volumes of parallelepipeds spanned by column vectors.
If $D \neq 0$, the vectors are linearly independent, ensuring a unique solution.

related_concepts.name: Consistent System
related_concepts.definition: A system of equations that has at least one set of solutions.

subject: Math
title: Cramer's Rule (No Solution)
description: Condition for inconsistent system (Parallel planes).
derivation:
If $D=0$, the coefficient matrix is singular (planes normals are coplanar/parallel).
If any numerator determinant ($D_x, D_y, D_z$) is non-zero, it implies a contradiction (like $0 \cdot x = 5$).
Geometrically, this corresponds to parallel planes with no common intersection.

related_concepts.name: Inconsistent System
related_concepts.definition: A system of equations with no solution.

subject: Math
title: Cramer's Rule (Infinite Solutions)
description: Condition for dependent system (Coincident or intersecting in a line).
derivation:
All determinants zero implies $0 \cdot x = 0$.
This creates a dependent system where equations are multiples of each other or linear combinations.
Result is a line or plane of solutions (infinite points).
*Note: Exception exists for parallel planes, requiring Gaussian check.*

related_concepts.name: Dependent System
related_concepts.definition: System with infinite solutions where one equation can be derived from others.

subject: Math
title: Factor Theorem
description: Useful for factorizing determinants containing variables.
derivation:
Based on polynomial theory.
If substituting $x=a$ makes two rows or columns identical, the determinant value becomes zero.
Since determinant expansion is a polynomial, by Factor Theorem, $(x-a)$ must be a factor of $\Delta(x)$.
Example: If rows are $1, x, x^2$ and $1, y, y^2$, then $(x-y)$ is a factor.

related_concepts.name: Vandermonde Determinant
related_concepts.definition: Determinant with terms $x_i^j$, factors into $\Pi(x_i - x_j)$.

subject: Math
title: Expansion (3×3)
visual_data: \Delta = \det \begin{pmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{pmatrix} = a_1(b_2 c_3 - b_3 c_2) - b_1(a_2 c_3 - a_3 c_2) + c_1(a_2 b_3 - a_3 b_2)
description: Expansion of a 3×3 determinant along the first row (Sarrus/cofactor). \(a_i,b_i,c_i\)=entries of the determinant.

subject: Math
title: Expansion via Cofactors
visual_data: \Delta = \sum_{j} a_{ij} C_{ij} \quad (\text{fixed row } i), \quad C_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j} M_{ij}
description: Value of a determinant as sum of products of elements and their cofactors along any one row/column. \(M_{ij}\)=minor, \(C_{ij}\)=cofactor of \(a_{ij}\).

subject: Math
title: False Expansion = 0
description: Sum of products of elements of one row with cofactors of a different row is zero. \(a_{ij}\)=element, \(C_{kj}\)=cofactor of another row.

subject: Math
title: Row/Column Interchange
description: Determinant is unchanged on transpose; swapping any two rows (or columns) flips the sign. \(R_i\)=row \(i\).

subject: Math
title: Zero Determinant Conditions
visual_data: \Delta = 0 \text{ if any row/column is all zeros, or two rows/columns are identical or proportional}
description: Standard situations giving a vanishing determinant. Identical or proportional lines \(\Rightarrow\) linear dependence \(\Rightarrow\Delta=0\).

subject: Math
title: Scalar Multiple of a Line
description: Multiplying every element of one row (or column) by \(k\) multiplies the determinant by \(k\). \(k\)=scalar.

subject: Math
title: Invariance Property
visual_data: R_i \to R_i + k R_j \implies \Delta \text{ unchanged} \quad (i \ne j)
description: Adding a multiple of one row/column to another leaves the determinant invariant (main simplification tool). \(k\)=any scalar.

subject: Math
title: Sum-Splitting Property
visual_data: \det \begin{pmatrix} a_1+x_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2+x_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3+x_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{pmatrix} = \det \begin{pmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{pmatrix} + \det \begin{pmatrix} x_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ x_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ x_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{pmatrix}
description: A determinant splits into the sum of two when one line is written as a sum of two columns/rows. Other lines stay identical.

subject: Math
title: Scalar Times Whole Determinant
description: Multiplying a whole \(n\times n\) matrix by \(k\) scales its determinant by \(k^n\). \(n\)=order of matrix.

subject: Math
title: Product of Determinants
description: Determinant of a product equals product of determinants (multiplied row-by-row or row-by-column). \(A,B\)=square matrices of same order.

subject: Math
title: Determinant of Powers
description: Determinant of integer powers and of the inverse. \(A\)=square matrix, \(k\in\mathbb{Z}\), needs \(\det A \ne 0\) for inverse.

subject: Math
title: Adjoint & Inverse
description: Inverse via adjoint; valid only when \(\det A \ne 0\) (non-singular). \(\text{adj}(A)\)=transpose of cofactor matrix, \(I\)=identity.

subject: Math
title: Determinant of Adjoint
description: Key adjoint identities for an \(n\times n\) matrix. \(n\)=order; for \(3\times3\): \(\det(\text{adj}\,A)=(\det A)^2\).

subject: Math
title: Adjoint of Product
description: Adjoint of a product reverses order; scaling rule for adjoint. \(A,B\)= \(n\times n\) matrices, \(k\)=scalar.

subject: Math
title: Diagonal / Triangular Determinant
visual_data: \det \begin{pmatrix} a_1 & 0 & 0 \\ * & a_2 & 0 \\ * & * & a_3 \end{pmatrix} = a_1 a_2 a_3
description: Determinant of a (upper/lower) triangular or diagonal matrix is the product of its diagonal entries. \(a_i\)=diagonal elements.

subject: Math
title: Skew-Symmetric (Odd Order)
description: Any odd-order skew-symmetric matrix is singular. \(A^T\)=transpose, \(n\)=order of matrix.

subject: Math
title: Collinearity of 3 Points
visual_data: \det \begin{pmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{pmatrix} = 0
description: Three points are collinear iff this determinant (twice the triangle area) vanishes. \((x_i,y_i)\)=the three points.

subject: Math
title: Line Through Two Points
visual_data: \det \begin{pmatrix} x & y & 1 \\ x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \end{pmatrix} = 0
description: Equation of the straight line joining \((x_1,y_1)\) and \((x_2,y_2)\) in determinant form. \((x,y)\)=variable point on line.

subject: Math
title: Cyclic Determinant
visual_data: \det \begin{pmatrix} a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b \end{pmatrix} = -(a^3 + b^3 + c^3 - 3abc) = -(a+b+c)(a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca)
description: Standard cyclic determinant; vanishes when \(a+b+c=0\) or \(a=b=c\). \(a,b,c\)=cyclically arranged entries.

subject: Math
title: Vandermonde Determinant
visual_data: \det \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ a & b & c \\ a^2 & b^2 & c^2 \end{pmatrix} = (a-b)(b-c)(c-a)
description: Classic factorable determinant; zero iff two of \(a,b,c\) are equal. \(a,b,c\)=the three parameters.

subject: Math
title: Homogeneous System (Nontrivial)
visual_data: AX = 0 \text{ has a nontrivial solution} \iff \det A = 0
description: A homogeneous linear system has solutions other than \(X=0\) iff its coefficient determinant vanishes. \(A\)=coefficient matrix.

subject: Math
title: Singular vs Non-Singular
description: Invertibility criterion: a matrix is non-singular iff its determinant is nonzero. \(A\)=square matrix.

subject: Math
title: Differentiation of a Determinant
visual_data: \frac{d}{dx}\det \begin{pmatrix} f_1 & g_1 \\ f_2 & g_2 \end{pmatrix} = \det \begin{pmatrix} f_1' & g_1' \\ f_2 & g_2 \end{pmatrix} + \det \begin{pmatrix} f_1 & g_1 \\ f_2' & g_2' \end{pmatrix}
description: Differentiate a determinant row-by-row (or column-by-column), one line at a time. \(f_i,g_i\)=functions of \(x\), prime = \(d/dx\).

subject: Math
title: Base Change Formula
description: Formula to convert logarithm to a new base $c$.
derivation:
Let $x = \log_a b \implies a^x = b$.
Take $\log_c$ on both sides:
$\log_c (a^x) = \log_c b$
$x \log_c a = \log_c b$
$x = \frac{\log_c b}{\log_c a}$.

related_concepts.name: Reciprocal Property
related_concepts.definition: $\log_a b = \frac{1}{\log_b a}$ (Setting $c=b$).

subject: Math
title: Base Power Rule
description: The exponent of the base comes out as a reciprocal fraction.
derivation:
Let $x = \log_{a^k} b \implies (a^k)^x = b$.
$a^{kx} = b$.
Convert to log base $a$:
$\log_a (a^{kx}) = \log_a b$.
$kx = \log_a b \implies x = \frac{1}{k} \log_a b$.

related_concepts.name: Argument Power Rule
related_concepts.definition: $\log_a (b^k) = k \log_a b$.

subject: Math
title: Fundamental Log Identity
description: Exponential and Logarithmic functions are inverses.
derivation:
Let $y = \log_a x$.
By definition of logarithm: $a^y = x$.
Substitute $y$ back into the exponent:
$a^{\log_a x} = x$.

subject: Math
title: Log Exchange Property
description: Base and argument can be swapped.
derivation:
Take $\log_c$ of LHS: $\log_c (a^{\log_c b}) = (\log_c b)(\log_c a)$.
Take $\log_c$ of RHS: $\log_c (b^{\log_c a}) = (\log_c a)(\log_c b)$.
Since the logs are equal (multiplication is commutative), the original values are equal.

related_concepts.name: Commutativity
related_concepts.definition: $xy = yx$.

subject: Math
title: Product, Quotient & Power Laws
visual_data: \log_a(mn)=\log_a m+\log_a n \\ \log_a\frac{m}{n}=\log_a m-\log_a n \\ \log_a m^p = p\,\log_a m
description: Basic logarithm laws used to split/combine logs. \(a>0,a\ne 1\); \(m,n>0\); \(p\) any real.
derivation:
Let \(\log_a m=x,\ \log_a n=y\Rightarrow m=a^x,\ n=a^y\)
Then \(mn=a^{x+y}\Rightarrow\log_a(mn)=x+y\)

subject: Math
title: Reciprocal Base Rule
description: Relates a log to its reciprocal with swapped base/argument. \(a,b>0\); \(a,b\ne 1\).
derivation: \(\log_a b=\frac{\log_c b}{\log_c a}=\frac{1}{\frac{\log_c a}{\log_c b}}=\frac{1}{\log_b a}\)

subject: Math
title: Chain Rule of Logs
description: Telescoping product of logs collapses to a single log. All bases/arguments \(>0\) and bases \(\ne 1\).
derivation: \(\log_a b\cdot\log_b c=\frac{\ln b}{\ln a}\cdot\frac{\ln c}{\ln b}=\frac{\ln c}{\ln a}=\log_a c\), extend by induction.

subject: Math
title: Generalized Power-Base Rule
description: Exponents on both base and argument come out as a ratio. \(a>0,a\ne 1\); \(b>0\); \(q\ne 0\).

subject: Math
title: Log Sign / Comparison Rule
description: Decides sign of a log from positions of base and argument relative to 1. \(a>0,a\ne1\); \(x>0\).

subject: Math
title: Log Inequality (base handling)
visual_data: \text{If } a>1:\ \log_a x>\log_a y\iff x>y \\ \text{If } 0<a<1:\ \log_a x>\log_a y\iff x<y
description: Direction of inequality flips when base lies in (0,1). \(a>0,a\ne1\); \(x,y>0\).

subject: Math
title: Logarithmic Equation Reduction
visual_data: \log_a x=b \iff x=a^{b}\quad(a>0,\ a\ne1) \\ \log_a f(x)=\log_a g(x)\iff f(x)=g(x)>0
description: Converts a log equation to exponential / argument form for solving. \(a>0,a\ne1\); arguments \(>0\).

subject: Math
title: Characteristic & Mantissa
description: Decomposes a common log into integer + fractional parts for digit counting. \(N>0\); mantissa always non-negative.

subject: Math
title: Number of Digits
description: Counts integer digits of a positive integer using its common log. \(N\) positive integer; \(\lfloor\ \rfloor\)=floor (greatest integer).
derivation: If characteristic of \(\log_{10}N\) is \(k\) then \(10^{k}\le N<10^{k+1}\Rightarrow N\) has \(k+1\) digits.

subject: Math
title: Leading-Zeros Rule
description: Counts zeros immediately after the decimal point before first significant digit. \(0<N<1\); characteristic is negative integer.

subject: Math
title: Natural Log & Series
visual_data: \ln x=\log_e x,\quad e\approx 2.718 \\ \log_{10} x=\frac{\ln x}{\ln 10}=\ln x\cdot\log_{10} e
description: Defines natural log and converts between natural and common logs. \(x>0\); \(\log_{10}e\approx 0.4343\).

subject: Math
title: Standard Log Values
description: Memorize these baseline log evaluations. \(a>0,a\ne1\); \(k\) any real.

subject: Math
title: First Principle of Induction
description: Logical skeleton of PMI: base case plus inductive step proves the statement for all naturals. \(P(n)\)=statement; \(k\) arbitrary natural.

subject: Math
title: Induction: Steps Template
visual_data: \text{Base: verify } P(n_0)\\ \text{Hypothesis: assume } P(k),\ k\ge n_0\\ \text{Step: prove } P(k)\Rightarrow P(k+1)
description: Standard 3-step procedure for any induction proof, starting from initial value \(n_0\). \(n_0\)=smallest valid \(n\) (often 1).

subject: Math
title: Sum of First n Naturals
description: Classic induction-provable summation. \(n\in\mathbb{N}\); \(r\)=running index.

subject: Math
title: Sum of Squares & Cubes
description: Standard power sums proved by induction; note cube sum = (sum of naturals)². \(n\in\mathbb{N}\).

subject: Math
title: Standard Divisibility Results
visual_data: n^{3}-n \text{ divisible by } 6 \\ 3^{2n}-1 \text{ divisible by } 8 \\ x^{n}-y^{n} \text{ divisible by } (x-y)
description: Frequently-asked induction divisibility statements. \(n\in\mathbb{N}\); \(x,y\) integers, \(x\ne y\).

subject: Math
title: Sum of First n Odd Numbers
description: Sum of first \(n\) odd naturals is a perfect square (classic PMI example). \(n\in\mathbb{N}\).

subject: Math
title: Telescoping Sum (1/r(r+1))
description: Standard telescoping result provable by induction. \(n\in\mathbb{N}\); \(r\)=index.
derivation: \(\frac{1}{r(r+1)}=\frac1r-\frac1{r+1}\Rightarrow\) sum telescopes to \(1-\frac{1}{n+1}=\frac{n}{n+1}\)

subject: Math
title: Strong Induction Principle
description: Complete (strong) induction: assume all prior cases to prove the next; used when recursion depends on several earlier terms. \(P(n)\)=statement.

subject: Math
title: Modulus Inequality (<)
description: Solution set for absolute value less than a positive constant.
derivation:
Case 1 ($x \ge 0$): $|x| = x$. So $x < a$. Combine: $0 \le x < a$.
Case 2 ($x < 0$): $|x| = -x$. So $-x < a \implies x > -a$. Combine: $-a < x < 0$.
Union of cases: $-a < x < a$.

related_concepts.name: Distance Interpretation
related_concepts.definition: Distance of x from 0 is less than a.

subject: Math
title: Modulus Inequality (>)
description: Solution set for absolute value greater than a positive constant.
derivation:
Case 1 ($x \ge 0$): $|x| = x$. So $x > a$.
Case 2 ($x < 0$): $|x| = -x$. So $-x > a \implies x < -a$.
Union of cases: $x \in (-\infty, -a) \cup (a, \infty)$.

related_concepts.name: Exterior Region
related_concepts.definition: Points strictly outside the interval $[-a, a]$.

subject: Math
title: Roots Relation
description: Sum and product of roots for $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$.
derivation:
Roots are $\frac{-b \pm \sqrt{D}}{2a}$.
Sum: $\frac{-b+\sqrt{D}}{2a} + \frac{-b-\sqrt{D}}{2a} = \frac{-2b}{2a} = -\frac{b}{a}$.
Product: $\frac{(-b)^2 - (\sqrt{D})^2}{4a^2} = \frac{b^2 - (b^2-4ac)}{4a^2} = \frac{4ac}{4a^2} = \frac{c}{a}$.

related_concepts.name: Newton's Sums
related_concepts.definition: $a S_n + b S_{n-1} + c S_{n-2} = 0$ where $S_n = \alpha^n + \beta^n$.

subject: Math
title: Nature of Roots
description: Discriminant determines the nature of roots.
derivation:
From Quadratic Formula $x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{D}}{2a}$:
1. $D > 0$: Two distinct real roots ($\pm$ gives diff values).
2. $D = 0$: Two equal real roots ($-b/2a$).
3. $D < 0$: Two complex conjugate roots ($\sqrt{-1} = i$).

related_concepts.name: Parabola Vertex
related_concepts.definition: The turning point of the graph is at $(-b/2a, -D/4a)$.

subject: Math
title: Condition for Common Root
description: Condition for one root common between $a_1x^2+b_1x+c_1=0$ and $a_2x^2+b_2x+c_2=0$.
derivation:
Let $\alpha$ be the common root.
$a_1 \alpha^2 + b_1 \alpha + c_1 = 0$
$a_2 \alpha^2 + b_2 \alpha + c_2 = 0$
Solve using Cramer's Rule (Cross-multiplication) for $\alpha^2$ and $\alpha$:
$\frac{\alpha^2}{b_1c_2-b_2c_1} = \frac{\alpha}{c_1a_2-c_2a_1} = \frac{1}{a_1b_2-a_2b_1}$.
Eliminate $\alpha$: $(\text{middle term})^2 = (\text{first})(\text{last})$.

related_concepts.name: Both Roots Common
related_concepts.definition: Condition: $\frac{a_1}{a_2} = \frac{b_1}{b_2} = \frac{c_1}{c_2}$.

subject: Math
title: Quadratic Formula
description: Roots of \(ax^2+bx+c=0\). \(a\)=leading coeff (\(a\neq 0\)), \(b\)=middle coeff, \(c\)=constant.

subject: Math
title: Roots via Discriminant
description: Roots and difference of roots in terms of \(D\). \(D=b^2-4ac\); difference taken up to sign.

subject: Math
title: Form Equation from Roots
description: Monic quadratic with given roots. \(\alpha,\beta\)=roots; sum \(=\alpha+\beta\), product \(=\alpha\beta\).

subject: Math
title: Nature of Roots Cases
visual_data: \begin{aligned} D>0 &: \text{real, distinct} \\ D=0 &: \text{real, equal} \\ D<0 &: \text{complex conjugate} \end{aligned}
description: Classification of roots by discriminant for real \(a,b,c\). \(D=b^2-4ac\).

subject: Math
title: Rational Roots Condition
description: Roots are rational iff \(D\) is a perfect square (rational coeffs). \(D=b^2-4ac\).

subject: Math
title: Irrational Roots Occur in Pairs
description: For rational coeffs, surd roots are conjugate. \(p,q\in\mathbb{Q}\), \(\sqrt{q}\) irrational.

subject: Math
title: Complex Roots Occur in Pairs
visual_data: p + iq \text{ root} \implies p - iq \text{ root}
description: For real coeffs, complex roots are conjugate. \(p,q\in\mathbb{R}\), \(q\neq 0\), \(i=\sqrt{-1}\).

subject: Math
title: Sum of Squares of Roots
description: Symmetric function used to build new equations. \(\alpha+\beta=-b/a\), \(\alpha\beta=c/a\).

subject: Math
title: Sum of Cubes of Roots
description: Symmetric function of roots. \(\alpha+\beta=-b/a\), \(\alpha\beta=c/a\).

subject: Math
title: Sum of Reciprocals of Roots
description: Used to form equation with reciprocal roots. \(\alpha\beta=c/a\neq 0\).

subject: Math
title: Difference of Roots (magnitude)
description: Absolute gap between roots. \(D=b^2-4ac\geq 0\) for real roots.

subject: Math
title: Both Roots Equal (D=0)
description: Repeated-root condition and its value. \(a\neq 0\); vertex abscissa \(=-b/2a\).

subject: Math
title: Sign of Quadratic (a>0)
description: Always-positive condition. With \(a<0,\,D<0\) the expression is always negative.

subject: Math
title: Maximum / Minimum Value
description: Extremum of \(f(x)=ax^2+bx+c\): min if \(a>0\), max if \(a<0\). \(D=b^2-4ac\).

subject: Math
title: Vertex Form
description: Completed-square form; vertex \(\left(-\frac{b}{2a},\,-\frac{D}{4a}\right)\). \(D=b^2-4ac\).

subject: Math
title: Roots of Opposite Signs
description: Real roots with opposite signs. Auto-implies \(D>0\). \(\alpha\beta=c/a\).

subject: Math
title: Both Roots Positive
description: Conditions for both roots \(>0\). All three must hold simultaneously.

subject: Math
title: Number k between Roots
description: \(k\) lies strictly between the roots. \(f(x)=ax^2+bx+c\); needs \(a\neq 0\).

subject: Math
title: Both Roots Greater than k
description: Both roots \(>k\). \(f(x)=ax^2+bx+c\); all three conditions required.

subject: Math
title: Roots in Interval (k1,k2)
description: Both roots inside \((k_1,k_2)\). \(f(x)=ax^2+bx+c\); all four conditions required.

subject: Math
title: Exactly One Root in (k1,k2)
description: One root inside the interval, one outside. \(f(x)=ax^2+bx+c\); sign change across endpoints.

subject: Math
title: More than Two Roots ⇒ Identity
description: A quadratic with 3+ roots is the zero polynomial. Key for 'find values' problems.

subject: Math
title: Both Roots Common
description: Two quadratics identical (proportional coeffs) share both roots. \(a_i,b_i,c_i\)=coeffs.

subject: Math
title: Reciprocal Roots Condition
description: Roots are reciprocals of each other. From \(\alpha\beta=c/a=1\).

subject: Math
title: Equal-Magnitude Opposite Roots
description: Roots are negatives of each other. From \(\alpha+\beta=-b/a=0\).

subject: Math
title: Roots in Ratio m:n
description: Roots in ratio \(m:n\) (i.e. \(\alpha/\beta=m/n\)). Derived from sum/product relations.

subject: Math
title: Roots Differ by d
description: Given gap \(d\) between roots. From \(|\alpha-\beta|=\sqrt{D}/|a|\).

subject: Math
title: Newton's Power-Sum Recurrence
description: Recurrence for \(S_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n\). \(S_0=2,\ S_1=-b/a\); \(\alpha,\beta\) roots of \(ax^2+bx+c\).

subject: Math
title: Range of Rational Function
description: Find range: cross-multiply, treat as quadratic in \(x\), force real \(x\) via discriminant \(\ge 0\) in \(y\).

subject: Math
title: Transform Roots: k·root
visual_data: ax^2 + kb\,x + k^2 c = 0 \ \text{has roots } k\alpha, k\beta
description: Scale roots by \(k\). Replace \(x\to x/k\) in \(ax^2+bx+c=0\).

subject: Math
title: Transform Roots: reciprocal
visual_data: c x^2 + b x + a = 0 \ \text{has roots } \frac{1}{\alpha}, \frac{1}{\beta}
description: Reverse coefficients to get reciprocal roots. Requires \(c\neq 0\).

subject: Math
title: Pseudo-Quadratic (Discriminant in Other Var)
description: Resolvability of homogeneous expression into linear factors. \(a,b,c\) treat as quadratic in \(x/y\).

subject: Math
title: Corner Point Theorem
description: The optimal value (max/min) of a linear objective function $Z = ax + by$ always occurs at a corner point of the feasible region.
derivation:
The feasible region is a convex polygon.
The objective function $Z = ax + by = c$ represents a family of parallel lines.
As we increase/decrease $c$, the line moves parallel to itself.
The maximum or minimum value is reached when the line just touches the last point of the region before leaving it.
This point is geometrically guaranteed to be a vertex (or an edge connecting two vertices).

related_concepts.name: Feasible Region
related_concepts.definition: The set of all points satisfying the system of linear inequalities.

subject: Math
title: Objective Function
description: Linear function whose optimum (max or min) is sought. \(Z\)=quantity to optimize (profit/cost), \(a,b\)=constants, \(x,y\)=decision variables.

subject: Math
title: Feasible Region
description: Set of all points simultaneously satisfying every constraint (incl. non-negativity); it is always convex. \(F\)=feasible region, points in \(F\)=feasible solutions, points outside=infeasible.

subject: Math
title: Optimal at Corner Point
description: Optimal value (when it exists) occurs at a vertex of the feasible region; evaluate \(Z\) at all corners and pick best. \((x_i,y_i)\)=corner points (vertices), \(Z\)=objective value at each corner.

subject: Math
title: Multiple Optimal Solutions
visual_data: Z(P_1) = Z(P_2) \implies Z \text{ optimal on segment } P_1 P_2
description: If two distinct corner points give the same optimal value, every point on the line segment joining them is also optimal (infinitely many solutions). \(P_1,P_2\)=corner points with equal optimal \(Z\).

subject: Math
title: Bounded vs Unbounded Region
description: A bounded feasible region always yields both a maximum and a minimum of \(Z\) at corner points; an unbounded region may fail to have one of them. \(Z\)=objective function.

subject: Math
title: Unbounded Region: Max Test
visual_data: ax + by > M \text{ has feasible points} \implies \text{no maximum}
description: For an unbounded region, the maximum \(M\) at corners is valid only if the open half-plane \(ax+by>M\) has NO common point with the feasible region; otherwise no maximum exists. \(M\)=largest corner value, \(ax+by\)=objective.

subject: Math
title: Homogeneous Equation
description: Represents a pair of straight lines passing through the origin.
derivation:
Let the two lines be $y - m_1x = 0$ and $y - m_2x = 0$.
Combined equation: $(y - m_1x)(y - m_2x) = 0$.
$y^2 - (m_1+m_2)xy + m_1m_2x^2 = 0$.
Compare with standard form divided by $b$:
$(a/b)x^2 + (2h/b)xy + y^2 = 0$.
Coefficients match: $m_1+m_2 = -2h/b$ and $m_1m_2 = a/b$.

related_concepts.name: Homogeneous Function
related_concepts.definition: A function where $f(tx, ty) = t^n f(x,y)$. Here degree n=2.

subject: Math
title: Angle Between Pair of Lines
description: Angle between the lines represented by $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0$.
derivation:
From line theory: $\tan \theta = \left| \frac{m_1 - m_2}{1 + m_1 m_2} \right|$.
Use algebraic identity: $(m_1 - m_2)^2 = (m_1+m_2)^2 - 4m_1m_2$.
Substitute sums/products: $(-2h/b)^2 - 4(a/b) = \frac{4h^2 - 4ab}{b^2}$.
$\sqrt{(m_1-m_2)^2} = \frac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{b}$.
Denominator $1 + m_1 m_2 = 1 + a/b = (a+b)/b$.
Result follows.

related_concepts.name: Perpendicularity
related_concepts.definition: $a+b=0$ (Sum of coeffs of $x^2$ and $y^2$ is zero).

subject: Math
title: Equation of Angle Bisectors
description: Combined equation of the pair of lines bisecting the angles between $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$.
derivation:
Let the lines be inclined at $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$.
Bisector angles are $\frac{\theta_1+\theta_2}{2}$ and $\frac{\theta_1+\theta_2}{2} + 90^\circ$.
Locus of point $P(x,y)$ (polar $r, \theta$) such that $2\theta = \theta_1+\theta_2$ or $2\theta = \theta_1+\theta_2 + 180$.
$\tan 2\theta = \tan(\theta_1+\theta_2) = \frac{m_1+m_2}{1-m_1m_2}$.
$\frac{2 \tan \theta}{1 - \tan^2 \theta} = \frac{-2h/b}{1-a/b}$.
Substitute $\tan \theta = y/x$: $\frac{2(y/x)}{1-(y/x)^2} = \frac{-2h}{b-a}$.
Simplifies to standard form.

related_concepts.name: Perpendicular Bisectors
related_concepts.definition: The angle bisectors of a pair of lines are always perpendicular to each other.

subject: Math
title: Condition for General Equation
description: Condition for $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ to represent a pair of lines.
derivation:
The general equation represents a pair of lines if the discriminant $\Delta$ of the conic is zero.
Determinant form:
$\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} a & h & g \\ h & b & f \\ g & f & c \end{vmatrix} = 0$.
Expansion of this determinant yields the standard condition equation.

related_concepts.name: Point of Intersection
related_concepts.definition: Found by partial differentiation: $\frac{\partial S}{\partial x} = 0, \frac{\partial S}{\partial y} = 0$.

subject: Math
title: Condition for Parallel Lines
description: When the homogeneous pair \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0\) represents two real coincident/parallel lines. \(a,b\)=coefficients of \(x^2,y^2\); \(h\)=half-coefficient of \(xy\). Lines are real & distinct if \(h^2>ab\), coincident if \(h^2=ab\), imaginary if \(h^2<ab\).

subject: Math
title: Condition for Perpendicular Lines
description: Lines of the homogeneous pair are perpendicular iff coeff. of \(x^2\) + coeff. of \(y^2\) = 0. Holds for both homogeneous \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0\) and general \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0\) pairs. \(a,b\)=coefficients of \(x^2,y^2\).

subject: Math
title: Slopes: Sum & Product
description: Sum and product of slopes of the two lines in \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0\). \(m_1,m_2\)=slopes; \(a,b\)=coeff. of \(x^2,y^2\); \(h\)=half coeff. of \(xy\). Obtained by dividing the equation by \(x^2\) and treating \(m=y/x\) as roots of \(bm^2+2hm+a=0\).

subject: Math
title: Angle Bisectors (General Pair)
description: Pair of angle bisectors of the general pair \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0\) with point of intersection \((x_1,y_1)\). Shifts the origin to the intersection point, reducing to the homogeneous bisector form. \(a,b\)=coeff. of \(x^2,y^2\); \(h\)=half coeff. of \(xy\).

subject: Math
title: Point of Intersection (General Pair)
visual_data: x_1 = \frac{hf - bg}{ab - h^2}, \quad y_1 = \frac{gh - af}{ab - h^2}
description: Intersection point of the two lines given by general second-degree pair \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0\). Found by solving \(\frac{\partial S}{\partial x}=0,\ \frac{\partial S}{\partial y}=0\). \(a,b,h,g,f\)=coefficients; valid when \(ab\ne h^2\).
derivation:
\(\partial_x S = 2ax+2hy+2g = 0\)
\(\partial_y S = 2hx+2by+2f = 0\)
Solve \(ax+hy+g=0,\ hx+by+f=0\) by Cramer's rule
\(x_1 = \frac{hf-bg}{ab-h^2},\ y_1 = \frac{gh-af}{ab-h^2}\)

subject: Math
title: Distance Between Parallel Pair
description: Distance between the two parallel lines of \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0\) (parallel case \(h^2=ab\)). \(a,b,c,g\)=coefficients; use \(f^2-bc\) and divide by \(b(a+b)\) form if \(a=0\). Requires the pair to be genuinely parallel.

subject: Math
title: Combined Equation from Two Lines
description: Single second-degree equation representing two given lines \(a_1x+b_1y+c_1=0\) and \(a_2x+b_2y+c_2=0\); just multiply them. Expanding gives the \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c\) form with matching coefficients.

subject: Math
title: Area of Triangle with a Line
description: Area of triangle formed by the line-pair \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0\) (through origin) and the line \(lx+my+n=0\). \(a,b,h\)=pair coeff.; \(l,m,n\)=line coeff. The two lines through origin and the third line bound the triangle.

subject: Math
title: Matrix (Determinant) Condition
visual_data: \Delta = \det\begin{bmatrix} a & h & g \\ h & b & f \\ g & f & c \end{bmatrix} = 0
description: Determinant form of the condition for \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0\) to represent a pair of straight lines. Expanding \(\Delta\) gives \(abc+2fgh-af^2-bg^2-ch^2=0\). \(a,b,c,f,g,h\)=coefficients of the general second-degree equation.

subject: Math
title: Circular Permutation
description: Number of ways to arrange $n$ distinct objects in a circle.
derivation:
Linear arrangement of $n$ items = $n!$.
In a circle, shifting all items one step clockwise results in the same arrangement.
There are $n$ such rotational shifts for every linear arrangement.
Total distinct circular arrangements = $\frac{n!}{n} = (n-1)!$.

related_concepts.name: Necklace Problem
related_concepts.definition: If clockwise and anti-clockwise are same (flip allowed), $N = \frac{1}{2}(n-1)!$.

subject: Math
title: Derangements
description: Number of ways to arrange $n$ items such that none appears in its original position.
derivation:
Using Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion:
Total permutations = $n!$.
Subtract cases where at least 1 is fixed, add back 2 fixed, etc.
$D_n = n! - \binom{n}{1}(n-1)! + \binom{n}{2}(n-2)! - \dots$
$D_n = n! (1 - \frac{1}{1!} + \frac{1}{2!} - \frac{1}{3!} + \dots)$.

related_concepts.name: Approximation
related_concepts.definition: $D_n \approx \frac{n!}{e}$ (nearest integer).

subject: Math
title: Number of Divisors
description: Total divisors of $n = p_1^a p_2^b p_3^c...$ (prime factorization).
derivation:
A divisor is formed by selecting prime factors.
For $p_1^a$, we can select $p_1$ with powers $0, 1, 2, ..., a$ ($a+1$ choices).
For $p_2^b$, we have $b+1$ choices.
By Fundamental Principle of Counting, multiply choices.

subject: Math
title: Permutation nPr
description: Number of ways to arrange \(r\) distinct objects out of \(n\) (order matters). \(n\)=total distinct objects, \(r\)=chosen, \(0 \le r \le n\).

subject: Math
title: Combination nCr
description: Number of ways to select \(r\) objects out of \(n\) distinct objects (order irrelevant). \(n\)=total, \(r\)=chosen.

subject: Math
title: Symmetry & Pascal Rule
description: Complementary selection identity and Pascal's recurrence for combinations. \(n\)=total, \(r\)=chosen.

subject: Math
title: Equal Combinations Result
visual_data: ^{n}C_{x} = {^{n}C_{y}} \implies x = y \;\text{ or }\; x + y = n
description: Standard JEE result for equating combination indices. \(n\)=total, \(x,y\)=lower indices.

subject: Math
title: Permutations of Like Objects
description: Arrangements of \(n\) objects when some are identical. \(n\)=total objects, \(p,q,r\)=counts of each type of identical object.

subject: Math
title: Permutations with Repetition Allowed
description: Number of \(r\)-length arrangements from \(n\) distinct objects when each may repeat (e.g. filling \(r\) places, each in \(n\) ways). \(n\)=choices per place, \(r\)=places.

subject: Math
title: Distribution into r Groups (Repetition)
description: Number of ways to distribute \(n\) distinct objects into \(r\) distinct boxes, each object having \(r\) choices. \(n\)=distinct objects, \(r\)=distinct boxes.

subject: Math
title: Selection of One or More (Distinct)
description: Number of ways to select at least one object from \(n\) distinct objects. \(n\)=distinct objects.
derivation:
Each object is either chosen or not \(\Rightarrow 2^{n}\) subsets.
Exclude the empty selection \(\Rightarrow 2^{n}-1\).

subject: Math
title: Selection from Identical Groups
description: Ways to select one or more from objects of which \(p\) are alike of one kind, \(q\) alike of another, etc. \(p,q,r\)=counts of each identical type.
derivation:
From each type choose \(0,1,\dots\) up to its count \(\Rightarrow (p+1)(q+1)\cdots\) ways.
Subtract the all-zero (empty) case.

subject: Math
title: Division into Unequal Groups
description: Ways to divide \(n\) distinct objects into named groups of unequal sizes \(p,q,r\). For distribution to \(3\) distinct persons multiply by \(3!\).

subject: Math
title: Total Number of Combinations
description: Sum of all combinations equals total subsets of an \(n\)-set. \(n\)=number of distinct objects.

subject: Math
title: Distribution of Identical Objects
description: Ways to distribute \(n\) identical objects into \(r\) distinct boxes allowing empty boxes (non-negative integer solutions of \(x_1+\cdots+x_r=n\)). \(n\)=objects, \(r\)=boxes.

subject: Math
title: Sum of Divisors
description: Sum of all divisors of \(N = p_1^{a}p_2^{b}\cdots\). \(p_i\)=prime factors, \(a,b\)=their exponents.

subject: Math
title: Number of Diagonals of Polygon
description: Number of diagonals of a convex polygon with \(n\) sides. \(n\)=number of vertices/sides.
derivation:
Lines joining any 2 of \(n\) vertices: \(^{n}C_{2}\).
Subtract the \(n\) sides \(\Rightarrow \frac{n(n-1)}{2}-n = \frac{n(n-3)}{2}\).

subject: Math
title: Points, Lines & Triangles
description: From \(n\) points of which \(m\) are collinear: number of distinct lines and triangles. \(n\)=total points, \(m\)=collinear points.

subject: Math
title: Rectangles & Squares in Grid
description: Number of rectangles and squares in an \(m \times n\) grid of unit cells (chess-board type). \(m,n\)=rows and columns of cells.

subject: Math
title: Exponent of Prime in n! (Legendre)
description: Highest power of prime \(p\) dividing \(n!\) (used for trailing zeros etc.). \(n\)=factorial argument, \(p\)=prime, \([\cdot]\)=greatest integer.

subject: Math
title: Multinomial: Selections (Generating)
description: Number of ways to select \(n\) items from \(r\) types (unlimited supply) via generating functions. \(n\)=items selected, \(r\)=types.

subject: Math
title: Sum of Numbers Formed by Digits
description: Sum of all \(n\)-digit numbers formed using \(n\) distinct nonzero digits (each used once). \(\Sigma d\)=sum of the digits, repunit has \(n\) ones.

subject: Math
title: Selecting r when p Always Included/Excluded
description: Choosing \(r\) from \(n\) when \(p\) specified objects are always included, or always excluded. \(n\)=total, \(r\)=chosen, \(p\)=fixed objects.
